CONCEPT

5.4 Input Tax Credit ★★★ HIGH

An uninterrupted and seamless chain of input tax credit (hereinafter, "ITC") is one of the key features of GST. ITC is a mechanism to avoid cascading of taxes — in simple language, "tax on tax." Under the earlier system of taxation, credit of taxes levied by the Central Government was not available as set-off for taxes levied by State Governments, and vice versa. Under GST, the entire supply chain is subject to tax levied by the Central and State Governments concurrently, and because both taxes belong to the same regime, the credit of tax paid at every stage is available as set-off for tax payable at every subsequent stage.

Key Definitions (Sec. 2, CGST Act, 2017)

  • Sec. 2(19) Capital Goods: goods the value of which is capitalised in the books of account of the person claiming ITC and which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business.
  • Sec. 2(34) Conveyance: includes a vessel, an aircraft and a vehicle.
  • Sec. 2(59) Input: any goods other than capital goods used or intended to be used by a supplier in the course or furtherance of business.
  • Sec. 2(60) Input service: any service used or intended to be used by a supplier in the course or furtherance of business.
  • Sec. 2(61) Input Service Distributor (ISD): an office of the supplier of goods or services or both which receives tax invoices towards receipt of input services (including sec. 9(3)/9(4) reverse-charge invoices) for or on behalf of distinct persons u/s 25, and is liable to distribute the ITC in respect of such invoices in the manner provided in sec. 20.
  • Sec. 2(62) Input tax: the central tax, State tax, integrated tax or Union territory tax charged on any supply of goods or services or both made to a registered person — including IGST on import of goods and tax payable under reverse charge u/ss. 9(3)/9(4) — but excluding tax paid under the composition levy.
  • Sec. 2(63) Input tax credit (ITC): the credit of input tax.
  • Sec. 2(119) Works contract: a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property, wherein transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution of such contract.

Sec. 16(1): Every registered person shall, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed and in the manner specified in sec. 49, be entitled to take credit of input tax charged on any supply of goods or services or both to him which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business, and the said amount shall be credited to the electronic credit ledger of such person.

Taxpoint — Who Is Entitled to ITC

A person is entitled to ITC only if:

  • the person is a registered person;
  • goods or services or both supplied to him are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business;
  • he satisfies the prescribed conditions; and
  • he claims ITC in the manner prescribed u/s 49.

Conditions to Be Satisfied Before ITC Can Be Claimed [Sec. 16(2)]

No registered person is entitled to ITC unless — (a) he is in possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier (or other prescribed tax-paying document); (aa) the supplier has furnished the invoice/debit note details in GSTR-1, and those details have been communicated to the recipient u/s 37; (b) he has received the goods or services or both; (c) subject to sec. 41, the tax charged on the supply has actually been paid to the Government — in cash, or through utilisation of admissible ITC; (d) he has furnished the return u/s 39 (GSTR-3B).

Condition (b) — Receipt of Goods or Services

  • Goods received in instalments: where goods against one invoice are received in lots or instalments, ITC can be taken only upon receipt of the last lot or instalment.
  • No ITC on advance payment: ITC is not available on advance payment without receipt of goods; it becomes available only in the month in which the goods (or final lot) are actually received.
  • Non-payment of invoice within 180 days: where a recipient fails to pay the supplier the value of supply plus tax within 180 days of the invoice date (other than reverse-charge supplies), an amount equal to the ITC availed must be added to his output tax liability, with interest, per Rule 37. On subsequent payment to the supplier, the recipient may re-avail the credit reversed.
  • Bill-to-Ship-to model: a registered person is deemed to have received the goods/services where the supplier delivers goods (or provides services) to any other person on the direction of, and before/during movement on behalf of, such registered person — whether by transfer of documents of title or otherwise. This is a tripartite arrangement: two transactions, three parties.

EXAMPLE — Goods Received in Instalments

A consignment of coal is dispatched from Kolkata to Mumbai using 5 trucks. Invoice issued to the recipient on 30 March 2026. Four trucks reached the claimant by 30 March 2026; the truck carrying the final lot reached only on 2 April 2026.

Answer: ITC for the entire consignment can be availed only in the month of April 2026 — the month of receipt of the last lot.

EXAMPLE — Bill-to-Ship-to

H Traders (Maharashtra) receives an order from R Traders (Maharashtra) for 50 tables, with instruction to ship them to P Hardwares (Kolkata), a customer of R Traders.

Leg 1 (H Traders → R Traders): H Traders bills R Traders and ships to P Hardwares per instruction. ITC is available to R Traders even though it never physically received the goods.

Leg 2 (R Traders → P Hardwares): R Traders is the supplier and P Hardwares the buyer; R Traders bills P Hardwares.

In an Ex-Works contract, property in goods passes to the buyer at the supplier's factory gate; handing the goods to the transporter (arranged by the buyer) is treated as "Deemed Receipt." The buyer may claim ITC immediately on such handover, even if the goods physically reach his premises later — Circular No. 241/35/2024-GST dated 31-12-2024.

EXAMPLE — Condition (c): Tax Actually Paid to Government

Mr. Vikram acquires a laptop of ₹1,00,000 + GST @ 18% (9% CGST + 9% SGST) for professional use, from X Ltd.

Answer: ITC of ₹9,000 each in CGST and SGST is not available to Vikram if X Ltd fails to pay the GST to Government. X Ltd may discharge its liability by (a) utilising its own balance ITC, (b) paying cash to Government's credit, or (c) any combination of the two.

Condition (d) and the Depreciation Bar [Sec. 16(3)]

Condition (d) requires that the return u/s 39 (GSTR-3B) has been furnished. Separately, where depreciation has been claimed on the tax component of the cost of capital goods/plant & machinery under the Income-tax Act, 1961, ITC on that tax component is not allowed.

EXAMPLE — Depreciation on Tax Component Bars ITC [Sec. 16(3)]

Mr. Vikram acquires a laptop of ₹1,00,000 + GST @ 18% (9% CGST + 9% SGST) for professional use.

Depreciation u/s 32 — Effect on ITC Availability
ParticularsOption 1: Without GST in CostOption 2: With GST in Cost
Asset acquired during the year1,00,0001,18,000
Depreciation @ 40%40,00047,200
Closing WDV60,00070,800
ITC available — CGST9,000Nil
ITC available — SGST9,000Nil

Answer: Vikram must choose one route — claim depreciation on the base value and take ITC (Option 1), or capitalise GST and claim higher depreciation while forgoing ITC (Option 2). He cannot have both.

Maximum Time Limit for Claiming ITC [Sec. 16(4)]

ITC on any invoice/debit note cannot be claimed after the earlier of — (a) 30th November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice/debit note pertains, or (b) the actual date of furnishing the relevant annual return (GSTR-9).

This time limit does not apply to re-availment of ITC that had been reversed for non-payment to the supplier within 180 days. Where registration is cancelled and later the cancellation is revoked, and ITC on an invoice was not time-barred on the date of the cancellation order, the person may still claim it in a return filed by the earlier of the 30th-November/annual-return date, or 30 days from the revocation order (for the intervening period) — whichever is later.

Documentary Requirements for Claiming ITC [Rule 36]

ITC may be availed on the basis of:

  1. an invoice issued by the supplier u/s 31;
  2. an invoice issued u/s 31(3)(f) (reverse charge self-invoice), subject to payment of tax;
  3. a debit note issued by the supplier u/s 34;
  4. a bill of entry (or similar Customs document) for assessment of IGST on imports;
  5. an ISD invoice / ISD credit note or any document issued by an ISD under Rule 54(1).

ITC is available only if all applicable particulars of Chapter VI are contained in the document and furnished in Form GSTR-2 — though where a document is missing minor particulars but still carries the amount of tax, description of goods/services, total value, GSTIN of supplier and recipient, and place of supply (for inter-State supply), ITC may still be availed. No ITC is available on tax paid under an order confirming demand on account of fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression of facts.

GSTR-2B linkage: No ITC is available on invoices/debit notes reportable u/s 37(1) unless the supplier has furnished them in GSTR-1 (as amended in GSTR-1A, or via IFF) and the details have been communicated to the recipient in Form GSTR-2B under Rule 60(7). ITC is not available if it is not reflected in the recipient's Form GSTR-2B.

Reversal of ITC for Non-Payment of Consideration [Rule 37]

A registered person who avails ITC but fails to pay the supplier the value of supply plus tax within 180 days from the invoice date must furnish the unpaid value/ITC details, and the corresponding ITC is added to his output tax liability for the month immediately following expiry of the 180 days. Interest is payable at a rate not exceeding 18%, from the date of availing the credit till the date the amount is added to output liability. The Sec. 16(4) time limit does not apply to re-availment of credit reversed under this Rule.

Value of supplies made without consideration (Schedule I) and value added under sec. 15(2)(b) are deemed "paid" for this 180-day test.

ITC on Sales-Promotion Schemes [Circular No. 92/11/2019 dated 07.03.2019]

  • "Buy One, Get One Free": not a free supply under sec. 7(1)(a) — in substance it is two (or more) individual supplies for a single combined price, i.e. two goods for the price of one. ITC remains available to the supplier for inputs, input services and capital goods used for such offers.
  • Discounts ("Buy more, save more" / volume discounts): staggered/periodic discounts satisfying sec. 15(3) are excluded from the value of supply, provided the recipient reverses ITC attributable to the discount, based on the supplier's document. The supplier remains entitled to full ITC on inputs, input services and capital goods used for the discounted supply.

Apportionment of Credit — Mixed Use [Sec. 17(1) / (2)]

Sec. 17(1) — business vs. non-business use: where goods/services are used partly for business and partly for other purposes, credit is restricted to the input tax attributable to the business purpose.

Sec. 17(2) — taxable vs. exempt supply: where goods/services are used partly for taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) and partly for exempt supplies, credit is restricted to the input tax attributable to the taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies).

Taxpoint — Value of Exempt Supply [Sec. 17(3)]

Value of exempt supply includes supplies taxable on reverse charge in the recipient's hands, transactions in securities, sale of land, and (subject to Schedule II para 5(b)) sale of building. It excludes Schedule III activities/transactions, except (a) Schedule III para 5 (sale of land, and sale of building subject to Schedule II para 5(b)) and (b) prescribed activities under Schedule III para 8(a) (supply of warehoused goods before clearance for home consumption).

For valuing exempt supply: land/building — value adopted for stamp duty; security — 1% of its sale value.

Circular No. 240/34/2024-GST dated 31-12-2024: an Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO) paying tax on restaurant services (or other notified services) under sec. 9(5) is not required to reverse its own ITC for inputs/services used to facilitate such supplies — but it cannot use that ITC to pay the sec. 9(5) liability, which must be paid in cash.

EXAMPLE — Apportionment of Common ITC (Mr. Akhil, March 2026)

ITC on inward supply ₹2,00,000; Taxable supply (excl. zero-rated) ₹10,00,000; Export/zero-rated supply ₹5,00,000; Exempt supplies ₹3,00,000; Reverse-charge inward supplies ₹2,00,000.

Computation of ITC Available to Mr. Akhil — March 2026
Particulars₹
Total Supply (A) [10,00,000 + 5,00,000 + 3,00,000 + 2,00,000]20,00,000
Taxable supply incl. zero-rated (B) [10,00,000 + 5,00,000]15,00,000
ITC on inward supply (C)2,00,000
ITC available [C × B / A]1,50,000
⚠ TRAP

Block Credit — ITC Not Available [Sec. 17(5)]

ITC is never available in respect of the following, regardless of business use:

  • (a) Motor vehicles for transporting persons with approved seating capacity ≤ 13 (incl. driver) — except when used for (A) further supply of such vehicles, (B) transportation of passengers, or (C) imparting driving training. (ITC is freely available for vehicles seating > 13.)
  • (aa) Vessels and aircraft — except when used for (i) further supply, transportation of passengers, or training on navigating/flying them, or (ii) transportation of goods.
  • (ab) General insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance of the motor vehicles/vessels/aircraft covered by (a)/(aa) — except where those vehicles/vessels/aircraft are themselves used for the purposes specified in (a)/(aa), or where received by a taxable person manufacturing such vehicles/vessels/aircraft, or supplying general insurance in respect of them.
  • (b) Food & beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic & plastic surgery, leasing/renting/hiring of motor vehicles/vessels/aircraft (unless covered by the (a)/(aa) exceptions), life insurance and health insurance — except where the inward supply is used to make an outward taxable supply of the same category, or as an element of a taxable composite/mixed supply.
  • (ii) Membership of a club, health and fitness centre.
  • (iii) Travel benefits to employees on vacation (leave/home travel concession) — the (b)/(ii)/(iii) block lifts where the employer is statutorily obligated to provide the benefit to employees under any law.
  • (c) Works contract services for construction of immovable property (other than plant & machinery) — except where it is an input service for further supply of works contract service.
  • (d) Goods or services received for construction of an immovable property (other than plant & machinery) on own account, even if used in the course/furtherance of business.
  • (e) Goods or services on which tax has been paid u/s 10 (composition levy).
  • (f) Goods or services received by a non-resident taxable person — except goods imported by him.
  • (fa) Goods or services used for obligations under Corporate Social Responsibility (sec. 135, Companies Act 2013).
  • (g) Goods or services used for personal consumption.
  • (h) Goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift or free samples.
  • (i) Any tax paid u/s 74 in respect of any period up to F.Y. 2023-24.
⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: THE SEC. 17(5) BLOCKED LIST IS EXHAUSTIVE, NOT INTUITIVE

THE TRAP: students assume "used for business" is enough for ITC, and remember only the motor-vehicle and food/catering blocks — missing CSR expenditure (fa), construction on own account even for business (d), and the seating-capacity carve-out nuance under (a).

THE TWIST: Sec. 17(5) blocks ITC on these categories even where the "used in course/furtherance of business" test of Sec. 16(1) is fully satisfied — it is a standalone override. Also, "Plant & Machinery" (the carve-out in (c)/(d)) specifically excludes land, buildings, other civil structures, telecommunication towers, and pipelines laid outside the factory premises — even though these may be capitalised.

ItemITC Position
Motor vehicle, seating capacity > 13 (incl. driver)Eligible, unconditionally
Motor vehicle, seating capacity ≤ 13Blocked, unless used for further supply / passenger transport / driving training
Truck / vehicle for transport of goodsEligible
Insurance/repair of a vehicle whose own ITC is blockedBlocked
Insurance/repair of a vehicle whose own ITC is availableEligible
Works contract for Plant & Machinery (incl. foundation/structural support)Eligible
Works contract for immovable property other than Plant & Machinery, capitalisedBlocked
Repairs to immovable property charged to P&L (not capitalised)Eligible
CSR expenditure u/s 135 Companies ActBlocked
Goods lost / stolen / destroyed / gifted / free sampleBlocked
"Buy One Get One Free" goodsEligible (treated as two supplies for one price, not a free supply)
Sec. 17(5) is an absolute bar — it overrides Sec. 16(1) even where the goods/services are genuinely used in the course of business.

Availability of Credit in Special Circumstances [Sec. 18]

  • Sec. 18(1)(a) — New registration (applied within 30 days): credit of inputs held in stock and inputs in semi-finished/finished stock, as on the day immediately preceding the date he becomes liable to pay tax.
  • Sec. 18(1)(b) — Voluntary registration u/s 25(3): same as above (inputs in stock / semi-finished / finished goods), as on the day preceding the date of grant of registration — capital goods are not covered.
  • Sec. 18(1)(c) — Ceasing composition levy (Sec. 10): credit of inputs in stock, semi-finished/finished stock, and capital goods, as on the day preceding the date he becomes liable u/s 9 — credit on capital goods reduced by a prescribed %.
  • Sec. 18(1)(d) — Exempt supply becomes taxable: credit of inputs in stock/semi-finished/finished stock relatable to that supply, and capital goods exclusively used for it, as on the day preceding the date it becomes taxable — capital-goods credit reduced by a prescribed %.

Time limit [Sec. 18(2)]: ITC under the above cannot be claimed after 1 year from the date of issue of the tax invoice relating to the supply.

Change in constitution [Sec. 18(3)]: on sale, merger, demerger, amalgamation, lease or transfer of business with specific provision for transfer of liabilities, unutilised ITC in the electronic credit ledger may be transferred to the successor business.

Composition levy / supply turns wholly exempt [Sec. 18(4)]: the registered person must pay (by debit to electronic credit/cash ledger) an amount equal to the ITC on inputs in stock, semi-finished/finished stock, and capital goods, reduced by a prescribed %, as on the day preceding the switch. Any ITC balance left after this payment lapses.

ITC Payable on Supply of Capital Goods / Plant & Machinery [Sec. 18(6)]

On supply of capital goods/plant & machinery on which ITC was taken, the registered person must pay the higher of — (a) ITC taken, reduced by a prescribed % points; or (b) tax on the transaction value u/s 15.

Exception: where refractory bricks, moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures are supplied as scrap, tax may be paid on transaction value alone. (Note: supply of metal scrap by an unregistered person to a registered person attracts reverse charge.)

Manner of Claiming Credit in Special Circumstances [Rule 40]

  • ITC on capital goods under sec. 18(1)(c)/(d) is claimed after reducing the tax paid by 5% per quarter (or part thereof) from the invoice date.
  • A declaration in Form GST ITC-01 must be filed electronically within 30 days of becoming eligible (extendable by the Commissioner).
  • Where the aggregate claim (CGST + SGST/UTGST + IGST) exceeds ₹2,00,000, the declaration must be certified by a practising Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant.
  • ITC claimed under sec. 18(1)(c)/(d) is verified against the supplier's GSTR-1/GSTR-1A/GSTR-4 on the common portal.
  • For sec. 18(6), the credit is reduced @ 5% per quarter (or part thereof) from the invoice date.

Transfer of Unutilised Credit [Rule 41 / Rule 41A]

  • Rule 41 — Sale/merger/demerger/amalgamation/lease/transfer of business: the transferor furnishes Form GST ITC-02 electronically requesting transfer of unutilised ITC. On demerger, ITC is apportioned in the ratio of the value of assets of the new units per the demerger scheme. A CA/CMA certificate confirming the specific provision for transfer of liabilities must accompany the request; the transferee accepts the details on the portal, after which the credit is credited to its electronic credit ledger.
  • Rule 41A — Multiple registrations within a State/UT (Rule 11): the registered person furnishes Form GST ITC-02A within 30 days of obtaining separate registration(s), to transfer unutilised ITC to the newly registered place(s) of business, in the ratio of value of assets held by each at the time of registration. The transferee accepts on the portal to receive the credit.

Manner of Reversal of Credit Under Special Circumstances [Rule 44]

Applicable to Sec. 18(4) (opting for composition / supply turning wholly exempt) and Sec. 29(5) (cancellation of registration):

  • Inputs in stock / semi-finished / finished goods: ITC computed proportionately from the corresponding invoices on which credit was availed.
  • Capital goods in stock: ITC involved in the remaining useful life in months is computed pro-rata, taking useful life as 5 years.
  • Where tax invoices for inputs in stock are unavailable, the amount is estimated on the prevailing market price on the effective date.
  • The determined amount forms part of output tax liability — furnished in Form GST ITC-03 (sec. 18(4) events) or Form GSTR-10 (cancellation of registration); details above a threshold require CA/CMA certification.
  • For Sec. 18(6) capital goods, the same pro-rata method applies; if it exceeds the tax on transaction value, the excess forms part of output tax liability, reported in GSTR-1.

EXAMPLE — Pro-Rata Reversal on Capital Goods [Rule 44(1)(b)]

Capital goods in use for 4 years, 6 months, 15 days; ITC taken on such capital goods ₹60,000. Useful life taken as 5 years (60 months).

Remaining useful life in months (ignoring part of a month) = 5 months.

Answer: ITC attributable to remaining useful life = ₹60,000 × 5/60 = ₹5,000.

ITC on Inputs & Capital Goods Sent for Job Work [Sec. 19]

  • The principal may take ITC on inputs/capital goods sent to a job worker, even if sent directly to the job worker without first being brought to the principal's place of business.
  • Inputs not received back (or not supplied from the job worker's place per sec. 143(1)(a)/(b)) within 1 year of being sent out are deemed supplied by the principal to the job worker on the day sent out (or, if sent directly, 1 year from the job worker's date of receipt).
  • Capital goods not received back within 3 years are similarly deemed supplied (counted from date of receipt by the job worker, if sent directly).
  • Exception: the 1-year/3-year time limits do not apply to moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures, or tools sent to a job worker.

Per sec. 143, the principal may send inputs/capital goods to a job worker (and onward to further job workers) without payment of tax, and must bring back / supply onward inputs (other than moulds/dies/jigs/fixtures/tools) within 1 year, and such capital goods within 3 years, of being sent out.

Conditions & Restrictions for Goods Sent to Job Worker [Rule 45]

  • Goods move under a delivery challan issued by the principal (or, job-worker-to-job-worker, endorsed/issued as prescribed).
  • Details of challans for goods sent/received during the "specified period" are reported in Form GST ITC-04 by the 25th of the month succeeding that period.
  • "Specified period": 6 consecutive months (April–Sept / Oct–March) where the principal's aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds ₹5 crore; otherwise, a full financial year.
  • Where goods are not returned within the sec. 143 time limit, they are deemed supplied by the principal on the day sent out, declared in GSTR-1, with tax and interest payable by the principal.

Input Service Distributor (ISD) [Sec. 20 / Sec. 21]

An Input Service Distributor is an office of a supplier that receives tax invoices for input services and distributes the CGST/SGST/UTGST/IGST credit on those services to units with the same PAN supplying taxable goods/services. The ISD mechanism covers input services only — not goods (inputs or capital goods) — and lets a Head Office apportion credit on common expenses among consuming units that it cannot itself utilise (since it makes no output supply).

  • Credit attributable exclusively to one recipient unit is distributed only to that unit.
  • Credit attributable to more than one recipient is distributed pro-rata on the turnover of those (operational, in the current year) recipient units in the relevant State/UT.
  • Credit of central tax is distributed as central tax or integrated tax; credit of integrated tax is distributed as integrated tax or central tax — by way of a prescribed distribution document, within prescribed time/conditions.
  • An office receiving such invoices (including reverse-charge invoices u/ss. 9(3)/9(4)) is required to be registered as ISD u/s 24(viii).
  • Sec. 21 — excess distribution: where the ISD distributes credit in excess/contravention of sec. 20, the excess is recovered from the recipients with interest, applying sec. 73/74 mutatis mutandis.

EXAMPLE — ISD Distribution (ABC Ltd.)

ABC Ltd.'s Corporate Office (Bangalore, registered as ISD) receives an invoice for software licence & maintenance used at all four locations (Bangalore, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata), showing ₹4 lakh Central tax, ₹4 lakh State tax and ₹7 lakh Integrated tax.

Answer: since the software is used at all four locations, the ₹15 lakh combined credit cannot be claimed at Bangalore alone — it is distributed to Bangalore, Chennai, Mumbai and Kolkata via an ISD invoice, as integrated tax credit, on the basis of turnover.

Availment of ITC [Sec. 41]

  • A registered person may avail credit of eligible input tax, as self-assessed, in his return; the amount is credited to his electronic credit ledger.
  • Where the supplier has not paid the tax payable on a supply, the recipient's ITC availed on it must be reversed with applicable interest. Once the supplier pays the tax, the recipient may re-avail the reversed credit.

⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: ITC UTILISATION ORDER (SEC. 49A)

THE TRAP: students set off CGST credit against SGST liability, or SGST credit against CGST liability, or forget to exhaust IGST credit before touching CGST/SGST credit.

THE TWIST: ITC of IGST must be utilised in full first — towards IGST, then CGST, then SGST/UTGST liability — before any CGST or SGST/UTGST credit is touched (Sec. 49A). CGST credit can never be used to pay SGST/UTGST liability, and SGST/UTGST credit can never be used to pay CGST liability — cross-utilisation between CGST and SGST is never permitted, only via IGST.

ITC of…Can be utilised, in order, for…
IGSTIGST liability → then CGST liability → then SGST/UTGST liability (must be fully exhausted before CGST/SGST credit is used)
CGSTCGST liability (never usable against SGST/UTGST liability)
SGST/UTGSTSGST/UTGST liability (never usable against CGST liability)
CGST credit ↔ SGST credit cross-utilisation is barred in both directions — the only cross-head bridge is IGST credit.

Quick MCQ

1. ITC is not available if depreciation is claimed on the ______ component of the cost of capital goods under the Income Tax Act.

(a) Base Value(b) Tax(c) Total Value (Base + Tax)(d) Installation Charges

Correct: (b) Tax. Sec. 16(3) provides that if the registered person has claimed depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods, ITC on that tax component is not allowed.

2. What is the time limit for a registered person to avail ITC in respect of an invoice or debit note for a financial year?

(a) 31st December of the next financial year(b) Date of filing Annual Return(c) 30th November following the end of the financial year or the date of filing relevant Annual Return, whichever is earlier(d) 30th November following the end of the financial year or the date of filing relevant Annual Return, whichever is later

Correct: (c). Sec. 16(4) restricts availment of ITC after the 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the actual date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

3. In case of supply of goods received in lots or instalments, ITC can be availed upon receipt of:

(a) First lot(b) Any lot(c) Last lot(d) 50% of the lots

Correct: (c). As per the first proviso to sec. 16(2), where goods are received in lots or instalments, the registered person is entitled to take credit only upon receipt of the last lot or instalment.

4. Which of the following conditions must be satisfied to avail ITC?

(a) Possession of Tax Invoice(b) Receipt of Goods/Services(c) Tax charged has been paid to the Government(d) All of the above

Correct: (d). Sec. 16(2) lists all four conditions: possession of invoice, receipt of goods/services, payment of tax to the Government, and furnishing of return.

5. ITC is BLOCKED u/s 17(5) on motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of:

(a) More than 13 persons (including driver)(b) Not more than 13 persons (including driver)(c) Any capacity if used for personal purpose(d) Both (b) and (c)

Correct: (d). ITC is blocked on motor vehicles for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity not more than 13 (including driver), unless used for the specified purposes; it is also blocked where used for personal consumption.

6. A principal sending inputs to a job worker must receive them back within ______, failing which it shall be deemed as a supply on the date of sending out.

(a) 3 years(b) 1 year(c) 180 days(d) 6 months

Correct: (b). Sec. 19(3) stipulates that inputs sent for job work must be received back within 1 year. For capital goods, the limit is 3 years.

7. If a recipient fails to pay the supplier the value of supply along with tax within ______ from the date of issue of invoice, the ITC availed must be added to output liability.

(a) 90 days(b) 3 months(c) 180 days(d) 1 year

Correct: (c). As per Rule 37, non-payment of consideration within 180 days requires reversal of ITC along with interest.

8. ITC is not available for goods lost, stolen, destroyed, or written off. This restriction is provided under:

(a) Section 16(2)(b) Section 17(5)(h)(c) Section 19(d) Rule 42

Correct: (b). Sec. 17(5)(h) specifically blocks credit for goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift.

9. Which of the following is true regarding the utilization of ITC?

(a) CGST credit can be used to pay SGST liability(b) SGST credit can be used to pay CGST liability(c) IGST credit must be exhausted first before using CGST/SGST credit(d) CGST credit can be used to pay IGST liability only after SGST credit is exhausted

Correct: (c). Sec. 49A mandates that ITC on account of integrated tax (IGST) must be utilized fully towards payment of IGST, CGST, or SGST/UTGST before utilizing central or state tax credit.

10. In case of supply of capital goods or plant and machinery on which input tax credit has been taken, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to:

(a) Tax on the transaction value of such capital goods(b) Input tax credit taken on such capital goods reduced by percentage points as prescribed (5% per quarter)(c) Higher of (a) or (b)(d) Lower of (a) or (b)

Correct: (c). Sec. 18(6) provides that the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken on the capital goods, reduced by such percentage points as may be prescribed, or the tax on the transaction value determined u/s 15 — whichever is higher.

CONCEPT

5.5 Computation of GST Liability ★★★ HIGH

Computing GST liability for a period has two moving parts: (1) working out eligible Input Tax Credit (ITC) head-wise (IGST / CGST / SGST-UTGST) from inward supplies, and (2) working out output tax liability head-wise from outward supplies (intra-State → CGST + SGST/UTGST; inter-State → IGST) — then setting off ITC against output liability in the legally prescribed order of utilisation, with any shortfall paid in cash via the electronic cash ledger.

Order of utilisation of ITC [Sec. 49(5) r.w.r. 88A]

ITC on account of IGST: (a) first towards payment of IGST; (b) then remaining credit, if any, towards payment of CGST / SGST / UTGST — in any order and any proportion.

ITC on account of CGST: (a) first towards payment of CGST; (b) then remaining credit, if any, towards payment of IGST.

ITC of CGST shall be utilised towards IGST only after exhausting ITC of IGST fully, and only before utilising ITC of SGST towards IGST. ITC of CGST shall never be utilised towards payment of SGST/UTGST.

ITC on account of SGST/UTGST: (a) first towards payment of SGST/UTGST; (b) then remaining credit, if any, towards payment of IGST.

ITC of SGST/UTGST shall be utilised towards IGST only after exhausting ITC of IGST fully, and only where the balance of ITC on account of CGST is not available for payment of IGST. ITC of SGST/UTGST shall never be utilised towards payment of CGST.

Summarised position — permissible cross-utilisation of ITC against each output head:

ITC available on account ofOutput liability – Integrated taxOutput liability – Central taxOutput liability – State/UT tax
Integrated tax(I) fully, first(II)(III)
(II) & (III): once IGST liability is paid off, the balance ITC of IGST may be used towards CGST and SGST/UTGST — in any order and in any proportion [Rule 88A].
Central tax(V)(IV)Not permitted
State tax / UTGST(VII)Not permitted(VI)
Mandatory pre-condition [Sec. 49A]: ITC of CGST or SGST/UTGST cannot be used for any output liability (I–VII) until ITC of Integrated tax has first been utilised completely.

Sec. 49A: the input tax credit on account of central tax, State tax or Union territory tax shall be utilised towards payment of integrated tax, central tax, State tax or Union territory tax, as the case may be, only after the input tax credit available on account of integrated tax has first been utilised fully towards such payment.

EXAMPLE — Rule 88A flexibility (IGST ITC exceeds IGST liability)

Output liability: IGST ₹1,000; CGST ₹300; SGST/UTGST ₹300 (Total ₹1,600). ITC available: IGST ₹1,300; CGST ₹200; SGST/UTGST ₹200 (Total ₹1,700).

State/UT tax0—2000
Total1,000300300100
Option 2
ITC on account ofUsed for IGSTUsed for CGSTUsed for SGST/UTGSTBalance ITC
Integrated tax (fully exhausted)1,0001002000
Central tax0200—0
State/UT tax0—100100

Answer: Both options fully discharge all output liability with zero cash outgo — Rule 88A allows the balance IGST credit to be split between CGST and SGST/UTGST in any order/proportion, so the head-wise carry-forward balance differs (Option 1: CGST c/f ₹100; Option 2: SGST/UTGST c/f ₹100) even though the total outcome is identical.

In Option 2 the registered person pays SGST in cash and accumulates unused ITC under CGST, because the balance IGST credit left after setting off the IGST liability was not routed in the most efficient order/proportion across CGST and SGST as Rule 88A permits.

EXAMPLE — IGST ITC alone covers all liabilities

Tax liability: IGST ₹100; CGST ₹100; SGST ₹100. ITC available: IGST ₹500 (a); CGST ₹50 (b); SGST ₹50 (c).

EXAMPLE — correct vs. wrong order (three options)

Tax liability: IGST ₹100; CGST ₹100; SGST ₹100. ITC available: IGST ₹150 (a); CGST ₹175 (b); SGST ₹150 (c).

Answer: Option 1 — ITC of CGST ₹125 and SGST ₹50 carried forward. Option 2 — ITC of CGST ₹75 and SGST ₹100 carried forward. Option 3 (wrong) — ITC of IGST ₹50, CGST ₹75 and SGST ₹50 carried forward; this is the wrong way to utilise ITC because ITC of IGST is not fully exhausted (the residual ₹50 of IGST credit is left idle) before utilising the own-head CGST/SGST credit.

EXAMPLE — M/s. Tech Corp (attempting to save IGST credit for future imports)

Output Liability: CGST ₹1,00,000; SGST ₹1,00,000. ITC Available: IGST ₹2,00,000; CGST ₹50,000; SGST ₹50,000.

Step 2No need to use CGST/SGST creditsUse IGST credit for the balance
ResultIGST credit: 0; CGST credit c/f: ₹50,000; SGST credit c/f: ₹50,000Violates law — Sec. 49A mandates IGST credit must be exhausted first

Answer: The registered person cannot utilise CGST/SGST credits to pay their own-head liabilities until the IGST credit is fully exhausted first.
