⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: DETERMINING CGST/SGST vs. IGST LIABILITY, AND CROSS-UTILISING ITC WRONGLY

THE TRAP: students (a) tax an inter-State supply as CGST+SGST or an intra-State supply as IGST, and (b) set off a surplus SGST/CGST credit against the other's liability (SGST credit → CGST liability, or vice-versa) whenever cash looks tight, or (c) use CGST/SGST credit before the IGST credit is fully exhausted "to keep IGST credit free for imports."

THE TWIST: place of supply decides the head — intra-State (supplier and place of supply in the same State/UT) → CGST + SGST/UTGST; inter-State → IGST only. ITC of CGST can only go to IGST (never SGST/UTGST); ITC of SGST/UTGST can only go to IGST, and only if CGST balance is unavailable (never to CGST). And under Sec. 49A, ITC of CGST/SGST cannot be used for anything until ITC of IGST is fully exhausted first — "saving" IGST credit for later by using CGST/SGST credit first (Illustration: M/s. Tech Corp, "Wrong Way") is a straight violation of law, not a valid planning choice.

1. As per Rule 88A, Input Tax Credit (ITC) on account of Integrated Tax (IGST) shall first be utilised towards payment of Integrated Tax, and the amount remaining, if any, may be utilised towards the payment of:

(a) Central Tax only(b) State Tax only(c) Central Tax and State Tax/Union Territory Tax in that order mandatorily(d) Central Tax and State Tax/Union Territory Tax in any order and in any proportion

Correct: d. ITC on account of IGST can be utilised towards payment of CGST/SGST/UTGST in any order and in any proportion after paying the IGST liability.

2. Mr. X has ITC balance in his CGST ledger. He can utilise this credit for payment of:

(a) CGST and SGST(b) CGST and IGST(c) IGST, CGST and SGST(d) CGST only

Correct: b. ITC on account of CGST shall be utilised first towards CGST, and then remaining towards IGST. It cannot be utilised towards payment of SGST/UTGST.

3. Sec. 49A mandates that ITC on account of Central Tax (CGST) or State Tax (SGST) can be utilised towards payment of IGST, CGST, or SGST only after:

(a) The output liability of IGST is fully paid(b) The ITC available on account of Integrated Tax (IGST) has first been utilised fully(c) The output liability of CGST is fully paid(d) The ITC on account of SGST is utilised fully

Correct: b. Sec. 49A states that credit of CGST/SGST/UTGST shall be utilised only after the ITC available on account of Integrated tax has first been utilised fully.

4. When utilising ITC to pay off liability, which of the following set-off is prohibited?

(a) IGST Credit → CGST Liability(b) CGST Credit → IGST Liability(c) SGST Credit → CGST Liability(d) SGST Credit → IGST Liability

Correct: c. Under the summarised position, "Output liability on account of Central Tax" cannot be paid using "Credit on account of State Tax/UTGST" (Not Permitted).

CONCEPT

5.6 Registration ★★★ HIGH

Registration is the most fundamental requirement for identifying tax payers and ensuring compliance. It gives a business a unique number from the tax authorities to collect tax on the government's behalf and to avail ITC on inward supplies. Without registration a person can neither collect tax from customers nor claim ITC.

Advantages: legal recognition as a supplier; legal authority to collect tax and pass on ITC to recipients; ability to claim and utilise ITC; seamless flow of ITC from suppliers to recipients at the national level.

Nature of registration & the GSTIN

Registration under GST is PAN-based and State/UT-specific — a supplier must register in each State/UT from which it effects supply, but is not liable to register in a State from which it makes only exempt/non-taxable supply. Registration is not tax-specific: one registration covers CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST and cesses together. Generally one GSTIN per State per PAN — branches in different States each need separate State-wise registration, but branches within the same State get a single registration (one place declared principal, others additional).

GSTIN — a 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number.

Digits 1–2: State code · Digits 3–12: PAN of the legal entity · Digits 13–14: entity code (registration number of that PAN-holder within the State) · Digit 15: checksum digit.

Example: 19 AAICM1234K 1 Z 2 or 06 AAICM1234K 1 ZT.

Persons liable for registration [Sec. 22]

Every supplier is liable to be registered in the State/UT, other than a special category State, from where a taxable supply is made, if aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds the specified threshold. In a special category State, the threshold is ₹10 lakhs.

⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: "SPECIAL CATEGORY STATE" HAS TWO DIFFERENT LISTS

THE TRAP: treating every State on the Constitution's special-category list as entitled to the ₹10 lakh GST-registration threshold.

THE TWIST: Article 279A(4)(g) of the Constitution lists 11 special category States: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir. But for GST registration purposes, only Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura are treated as special category States (₹10 lakh threshold). Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand etc. follow the general threshold (Illustration 128 turns on exactly this distinction).

Category of supplierThreshold limit (general States)Threshold limit (special category States — Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura)
Exclusive supplier of goods (not in the specified-goods list below, and not located in the excluded States below)₹40,00,000₹10,00,000 (special category threshold governs)
Supplier of services, or supplier of both goods and services₹20,00,000₹10,00,000
Supplier of Ice-cream & other edible ice, Pan Masala, Tobacco & manufactured tobacco substitutes, fly ash bricks/aggregate (≥90% fly ash), Fly ash blocks, Bricks of fossil meals/similar siliceous earths, Building bricks, Earthen/roofing tiles₹20,00,000 (enhanced ₹40L limit not available)₹10,00,000
Persons engaged in intra-State supplies in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Tripura, Uttarakhand (even if exclusive goods suppliers)₹20,00,000 (enhanced ₹40L limit not available)—
Persons liable to compulsory registration u/s 24, or exercising the option of voluntary registration u/s 25(3)No threshold — registration required irrespective of turnover

Taxpoint: an aggregatist — a supplier is considered exclusively engaged in supply of goods even if it also supplies exempted services by way of extending deposits, loans or advances, to the extent the consideration is interest or discount.

Aggregate turnover [Sec. 2(6)]

"Aggregate turnover" means the aggregate value, computed on an all-India basis, of: (a) all taxable supplies (excluding the value of inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge); (b) exempt supplies (excluding exempted services by way of extending deposits, loans or advances where the consideration is interest or discount); (c) exports of goods or services or both; and (d) inter-State supplies of persons having the same PAN (e.g. stock transfers between branches) — but it excludes central tax, State tax, Union territory tax, integrated tax and cess.

  • Includes all supplies made by the taxable person, whether on his own account or on behalf of all his principals.
  • Excludes from a registered job worker's own aggregate turnover the value of goods supplied by him after job work — that supply is treated as a supply by the principal u/s 143.

"Exempt supply" [Sec. 2(47)] = supply attracting nil rate of tax, or wholly exempt u/s 11 (CGST) or Sec. 6 (IGST), and includes non-taxable supply. "Non-taxable supply" [Sec. 2(78)] = a supply not leviable to tax under the CGST Act or the IGST Act. For GST purposes, Delhi and Puducherry are treated as States.

Persons not liable for registration [Sec. 23]

  • (a) Any person engaged exclusively in supplying goods/services not liable to tax, or wholly exempt from tax, under the CGST Act or the IGST Act.
  • (b) Agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land. An agriculturist supplying other products beyond the applicable threshold must register. "Agriculturist" [Sec. 2(7)] = an individual or HUF cultivating land by own labour, by family labour, or by hired/servant labour under personal supervision of the individual or a family member.

Taxpoint — further categories notified as exempt from registration:

  1. Persons rendering taxable services who are liable to GST under reverse charge.
  2. Job-workers making inter-State supply of services to a registered person — except where liable u/s 22(1), or opting for voluntary registration, or engaged in supply of services relating to jewellery, goldsmiths' and silversmiths' wares.
  3. Persons effecting inter-State supplies of taxable services — where aggregate value on a PAN-India basis does not exceed ₹20 lakhs a year (₹10 lakhs for Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura).
  4. Persons effecting inter-State taxable supplies of handicraft goods — same ₹20 lakh / ₹10 lakh PAN-India threshold.
  5. Persons supplying services through e-commerce and liable to collect tax at source, provided aggregate turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh for the four special category States). "Electronic commerce operator" [Sec. 2(45)] = any person owning/operating/managing a digital or electronic facility/platform for electronic commerce.
  6. Casual taxable persons making taxable supplies of handicraft goods — same ₹20 lakh / ₹10 lakh PAN-India threshold. "Casual taxable person" [Sec. 2(20)] = a person occasionally undertaking supply of goods/services in a State/UT where he has no fixed place of business.
  7. The basic limit for mandatory registration has been raised from ₹20 lakhs to ₹40 lakhs for persons exclusively supplying goods, except: (a) persons requiring compulsory registration u/s 24; (b) suppliers of the specified goods (ice cream, pan masala, aerated water, tobacco, fly ash bricks etc.); (c) persons making intra-State supplies in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Tripura, Uttarakhand; and (d) persons who have opted for voluntary registration u/s 25(3) or wish to continue an existing registration.

Transfer of Business [Sec. 22(3)/(4)]

  • Where a registered person's business is transferred as a going concern (succession or otherwise), the transferee/successor is liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession.
  • On transfer pursuant to a scheme of amalgamation or demerger sanctioned by a High Court/Tribunal, the transferee is liable to be registered from the date the Registrar of Companies issues the certificate of incorporation giving effect to that order.

Compulsory registration in certain cases [Sec. 24]

The following categories must register irrespective of turnover size:

Category of personsExemption available
Persons making any inter-State taxable supplyInter-State supplies of taxable services, and inter-State supplies of handicraft goods, when turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakhs (₹10 lakhs special category)
Casual taxable persons making taxable supplyCasual taxable persons making taxable supplies of handicraft goods, if aggregate turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakhs (₹10 lakhs special category)
Persons required to pay tax under reverse charge—
Persons required to pay tax u/s 9(5) (e-commerce operator, for intra-State supplies of specified services through it)—
Non-resident taxable persons making taxable supply [Sec. 2(77): a person occasionally undertaking supply, with no fixed place of business or residence in India]—
Persons required to deduct tax u/s 51—
Persons supplying goods/services on behalf of other registered taxable persons, as agent or otherwise—
Input Service Distributors—
Persons supplying goods and/or services (other than u/s 9(5) supplies) through an e-commerce operator who must collect tax at source u/s 52Persons supplying services through e-commerce with aggregate turnover not exceeding ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh special category)
Every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source u/s 52—
Every person supplying Online Information and Database Access or Retrieval services (OIDAR) from outside India to a person in India, other than a registered taxable person—
Such other notified person—

Taxpoint — suppliers of goods through an e-commerce operator (who collects tax at source u/s 52) are exempted from registration if aggregate turnover in the preceding and current FY is within the sec. 22(1) threshold, subject to: (i) no inter-State supply of goods; (ii) supply through the e-commerce operator in only one State/UT; (iii) must hold a PAN; (iv) must declare PAN, business address and State/UT on the common portal before any supply; (v) must obtain an enrolment number on successful PAN validation; (vi) not more than one enrolment number per State/UT; (vii) no supply until the enrolment number is granted; (viii) the enrolment number ceases to be valid once regular registration u/s 25 is granted.

Special procedures notified for e-commerce operators: for supplies made by unregistered persons exempted from registration [Notification No. 37/2023] — the operator may allow supply only if an enrolment number is allotted, must not allow inter-State supply through it, must not collect TCS u/s 52(1) on such supplies, and must report the supplies in FORM GSTR-8. For supplies made by composition taxpayers [Notification No. 36/2023] — the operator must not allow inter-State supply, but must collect TCS u/s 52(1) and report in FORM GSTR-8.

Procedure for registration [Sec. 25 & Rule 8]

  • A person liable u/s 22 or 24 must apply for registration in every State/UT where liable, within 30 days of becoming liable.
  • A casual taxable person or non-resident taxable person must apply at least 5 days prior to commencement of business.
  • An SEZ unit / SEZ developer needs a separate registration, distinct from any place of business located outside the SEZ in the same State/UT.
  • Supply from the territorial waters of India is registered in the coastal State/UT nearest to the appropriate baseline.
  • A person is granted a single registration per State/UT, but may get separate registration for each place of business within a State/UT, subject to conditions [Rule 11].
  • Voluntary registration u/s 25(3) is allowed even if not otherwise liable; once registered, all provisions applicable to a registered person apply.
  • Each registration held by a person (single or multiple States) is treated as a distinct person for the Act's purposes; establishments in different States/UTs are treated as establishments of distinct persons.
  • PAN is mandatory for registration; a person required to deduct tax u/s 51 may instead use a TAN.

Application: declare PAN, mobile number, e-mail and State/UT in Part A of FORM GST REG-01 on the common portal → PAN validated online and OTP-verified → Temporary Reference Number (TRN) generated → Part B of FORM GST REG-01 submitted electronically with documents, using the TRN → acknowledgement issued in FORM GST REG-02.

This Part-A route does not apply to: a non-resident taxable person; a person required to deduct tax u/s 51; a person required to collect tax u/s 52; a person supplying OIDAR from outside India to a non-taxable online recipient; a person supplying online money gaming from outside India. Every Input Service Distributor must make a separate registration application as such.

Verification & approval [Rule 9]: registration approved within 7 working days of submission, in the ordinary case.

Extended to 30 days (with physical verification of the place of business) where: Aadhaar authentication is not undergone/opted for; the applicant, though Aadhaar-authenticated, is flagged for physical verification on data-analysis/risk parameters; or the proper officer (with Assistant-Commissioner-level approval) decides physical verification is warranted. If deficient, notice issued in FORM GST REG-03 within 7 working days; applicant replies in FORM GST REG-04 within 7 working days; if satisfied, officer approves within a further 7 working days; if not satisfied or no reply, application rejected in FORM GST REG-05. If the officer takes no action within the applicable period, the application is deemed approved.

Electronic (fast-track) registration [Rule 9A]: registration granted within 3 working days where the applicant opts for Aadhaar authentication, is identified as low-risk, and monthly output tax liability towards registered persons (B2B) does not exceed ₹2,50,000.

Mandatory withdrawal [Rule 14A] via FORM GST REG-32 once monthly B2B liability exceeds ₹2,50,000; a minimum of 3 months'/one tax period's pending returns must be furnished first [Notification No. 18/2025 – Central Tax].

Issue of certificate & effective date [Rule 10]: certificate in FORM GST REG-06 with a 15-digit GSTIN (2 State-code + 10 PAN/TAN + 2 entity code + 1 checksum).

If applied within 30 days of becoming liable → effective date = date of becoming liable. If applied after 30 days → effective date = date of grant of registration.

Aadhaar authentication [Sec. 25(6A)–(6D)]: an existing registered person must undergo Aadhaar authentication (or furnish proof of possession, or alternate identification if no Aadhaar is assigned) — failure deems the registration invalid. Every new individual applicant, and (for non-individuals) the Karta/Managing Director/whole-time Director/specified partners/Members of Managing Committee/authorised signatory etc., must similarly undergo authentication or furnish alternate identification. These Aadhaar provisions do not apply to a non-citizen of India, or to a class of person other than an individual/authorised signatory/managing-authorised partner/karta of an HUF.

Other procedural rules: Bank account details [Rule 10A] must be furnished within 30 days of grant of registration, or before filing GSTR-1/IFF u/s 37, whichever is earlier. Physical verification of premises [Rule 25], where required, is uploaded in FORM GST REG-30 within 15 working days after verification (or at least 5 working days before the Rule 9 time-limit expires, if verification precedes grant). A Temporary Identification Number [Rule 16A] — distinct from the TRN — may be granted by the proper officer to a person not liable to register but required to make a payment (e.g. a penalty), via an order in Part B of FORM GST REG-12 [Notification No. 07/2025 – Central Tax]. A Unique Identity Number [Rule 17] is granted (via FORM GST REG-13, certificate in FORM GST REG-06, within 3 working days) to UN agencies/multilateral bodies/foreign consulates/embassies and other notified persons. Every registered person must display the registration certificate and GSTIN on a name board at the principal and every additional place of business [Rule 18].

Deemed registration [Sec. 26]

Grant of registration/UIN under the SGST or UTGST Act is deemed to be a grant under the CGST Act too, provided the application has not been rejected within the Sec. 25(10) time limit; similarly a rejection under the SGST/UTGST Act is deemed a rejection under the CGST Act.

Casual taxable person & non-resident taxable person [Sec. 27]

  • Certificate of registration is valid for the period specified in the application, or 90 days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier — extendable, on sufficient cause, by a further period not exceeding 90 days.
  • Such person must make an advance deposit of tax equal to estimated tax liability for the registration period at the time of applying (and an additional deposit if seeking extension); the deposit is credited to the electronic cash ledger and utilised u/s 49.
  • A casual taxable person applies at least 5 days before commencing business, using the normal FORM GST REG-01 (no special form); acknowledgement is issued only after the advance deposit is made, using a temporary reference number.

Amendment of registration [Sec. 28]

A registered person (or UIN holder) must inform the proper officer of changes to the information furnished at registration, who may approve or reject the amendment (with an opportunity of being heard before any rejection). Approval is not required for certain prescribed particulars.

Taxpoint: Core-field amendments (business/legal name where PAN is unchanged, addition/deletion of stakeholders, principal/additional place of business other than a change of State) require an application within 15 days of the event, with the officer approving within a further 15 days. Non-core-field amendments (e-mail ID, mobile number, etc.) need no officer approval.

Cancellation / suspension of registration [Sec. 29]

  • The proper officer may cancel registration (own motion, or on application by the registered person / legal heirs on death) where: the business is discontinued/transferred/amalgamated/demerged/otherwise disposed of; there is a change in constitution; or the person is no longer liable u/s 22/24 or wishes to opt out of voluntary registration u/s 25(3). Registration may be suspended during pendency of such cancellation proceedings.
  • The officer may cancel from any date (including retrospectively) where: prescribed provisions are contravened; a composition taxpayer (Sec. 10) has not filed returns for a financial year beyond 3 months from due date; any other registered person has not furnished returns for 6 continuous tax periods; a voluntarily-registered person has not commenced business within 6 months of registration; or registration was obtained by fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression of facts — but only after giving an opportunity of being heard.
  • Cancellation does not affect liability for tax/dues for the period before cancellation. Cancellation under the SGST/UTGST Act is deemed cancellation under the CGST Act too.
  • On cancellation, the registered person must pay (by debit to electronic credit/cash ledger) an amount equal to the higher of: ITC on inputs held in stock, inputs in semi-finished/finished goods, or capital goods/plant & machinery, as on the day preceding cancellation; or the output tax payable on such goods. For capital goods/plant & machinery, the amount is ITC taken thereon reduced by prescribed % points, or tax on transaction value u/s 15, whichever is higher.

Grounds for cancellation [Rule 21]: not conducting business from the declared place; issuing invoices/bills without actual supply; violating Sec. 171 (anti-profiteering); violating Rule 10A (bank account details); availing ITC in violation of Sec. 16; over-declaring outward supplies in GSTR-1/1A versus the return u/s 39; or violating Rule 23(1)'s third/fourth proviso or Rule 86B (which caps use of the electronic credit ledger at 99% of output tax liability in a month where taxable supply, other than exempt/zero-rated, exceeds ₹50 lakhs).

Suspension [Rule 21A]: deemed-suspended from the date of applying for cancellation (or the date sought, if later), pending completion of cancellation proceedings; or suspended by the officer where he has reason to believe cancellation is warranted, or where return-comparison (GSTR-1/1A vs GSTR-3B, or inward-supply anomalies) or a Rule 10A contravention show significant discrepancies — intimated in FORM GST REG-31, with 30 days to explain. A suspended person cannot issue tax invoices, charge tax, claim refunds, or is required to file returns during suspension. Suspension is revoked on completion of Rule 22 proceedings (effective from the original suspension date); for non-filing/Rule-10A suspensions specifically, it is deemed revoked on furnishing all pending returns / complying with Rule 10A.

Cancellation process [Rule 22]: show-cause notice in FORM GST REG-17 (7 working days to reply in FORM REG-18); cancellation order in FORM GST REG-19 within 30 days of the application/reply; if the reply is satisfactory, proceedings are dropped via FORM GST REG-20 (also where pending returns are filed with full tax, interest and late fee).

Revocation of cancellation [Sec. 30 & Rule 23]

A person whose registration was cancelled on the proper officer's own motion may apply for revocation within 90 days of the cancellation order (extendable up to 180 days by the Additional/Joint Commissioner or Commissioner). No revocation application is allowed for a return-non-filing cancellation unless the returns are filed and tax/interest/penalty/late fee dues are paid; all returns for the period from cancellation to revocation must then be filed within 30 days of the revocation order. Officer either revokes (FORM GST REG-22, within 30 days of the application, for recorded reasons) or rejects (FORM GST REG-05) after issuing a show-cause notice (FORM GST REG-23, 7 working days to reply in FORM GST REG-24) and disposing the application within 30 days of receiving the reply.

ILLUSTRATION 122 — Registration requirements in independent cases

(a) Mr. Khan of West Bengal supplies tobacco-based Pan Masala, aggregate turnover ₹24 lakhs. (b) Mr. Tipati of Mizoram supplies papers, aggregate turnover ₹13 lakhs — would the answer differ if located in Meghalaya?

Answer: (a) For pan masala/tobacco/manufactured tobacco substitutes etc., the threshold is ₹20 lakhs (the enhanced ₹40 lakh limit does not apply) — Mr. Khan is liable to register mandatorily. (b) In Mizoram the threshold is ₹10 lakhs, so Mr. Tipati is liable to register. If located in Meghalaya, the threshold is ₹20 lakhs, so he would not be liable to register.

ILLUSTRATION 123 — Effective date of registration

M Ltd. (taxable supply of services, Karnataka) exceeded the ₹20 lakh threshold on 25-08-2025. (a) Applies 15-09-2025, granted 30-09-2025. (b) Applies 28-09-2025, granted 06-10-2025.

Answer: where the application is submitted within 30 days of becoming liable, the effective date is the date of becoming liable; otherwise it is the date of grant. (a) Application made within 30 days → effective date 25-08-2025. (b) Application made after 30 days → effective date 06-10-2025.

ILLUSTRATION 124 — Mr. Vishnu, Tamil Nadu, F.Y. 2024-25 (aggregate turnover for registration)

Sale of diesel taxed under State VAT ₹7,00,000; supply of goods, after completion of job work, from Mr. Vishnu's premises directly by his principal (Vishnu registered as job worker) ₹4,20,000; export supply to Dubai ₹6,00,000; supply to his own additional place of business in Tamil Nadu under the same registration ₹5,00,000; supply of goods exempt from GST ₹8,20,000.

Computation of aggregate turnover for CGST registration
Particulars₹
Sale of diesel taxed under State VAT (non-taxable supply per Sec. 2(47) — still includible)7,00,000
Supply of goods, after job work, directly by the principal (treated as supply by the principal per Explanation (ii) to Sec. 22)Nil
Export supply to Dubai (specifically includible per Sec. 2(6))6,00,000
Supply to own additional place of business in Tamil Nadu (supply without consideration to a unit within the same State/registration is not a "supply")Nil
Supply of goods exempt from GST (exempt supply is includible per Sec. 2(47))8,20,000
Aggregate turnover for CGST registration purposes21,20,000

Answer: Since aggregate turnover (₹21,20,000) exceeds ₹20 lakh, Mr. Vishnu must register. Also, since he makes an export supply, he makes an inter-State taxable supply and is liable for compulsory registration u/s 24 regardless of whether the threshold is crossed.

ILLUSTRATION 125 — Electronic registration & withdrawal

Mr. Arjun, a Cost Accountant starting practice in Pune, opts for Aadhaar authentication and is identified as "Low Risk"; estimated monthly B2B output tax liability ₹1,80,000. Six months later, his monthly B2B liability reaches ₹3,00,000.

Answer: (1) Since he is Aadhaar-authenticated, low risk, and his B2B liability (₹1.8L) is below ₹2,50,000, he qualifies for electronic registration under Rule 9A — registration granted within 3 working days. (2) Since his liability (₹3L) now exceeds ₹2,50,000, he must mandatorily withdraw from Rule 9A via FORM GST REG-32, after ensuring all pending returns (minimum 3 months/one tax period) are furnished.

ILLUSTRATION 126 — Temporary Identification Number vs. TRN

(a) Mr. X applies for fresh GST registration and verifies mobile/e-mail on the portal. (b) Mr. Y, unregistered, is caught transporting goods without documents; not liable for regular registration but wishes to pay a ₹50,000 penalty to release his goods.

Answer: (a) The number generated after mobile/e-mail verification is the Temporary Reference Number (TRN), used solely to access and fill Part B of the application. (b) Mr. Y needs to make a payment without being liable to register — the proper officer grants him a Temporary Identification Number (distinct from the TRN) via an order in Part B of FORM GST REG-12 to facilitate the penalty payment.

ILLUSTRATION 127 — Comparison of registration timelines

Case A: Aadhaar-authenticated but monthly B2B tax liability ₹5,00,000. Case B: Aadhaar-authenticated, Low Risk, monthly B2B liability ₹1,00,000. Case C: fails to undergo Aadhaar authentication.

Answer: Case A — liability exceeds ₹2.5 lakhs so Rule 9A does not apply; standard Rule 9 timeline of 7 working days. Case B — meets Rule 9A criteria (low risk + liability ≤ ₹2.5 lakhs); granted within 3 working days. Case C — no Aadhaar authentication, so physical verification may be required; granted within 30 days after verification.

ILLUSTRATION 128 — "Healthy Foods," Assam (aggregate turnover & exemption threshold)

Exclusively supplies: exempted agro-products ₹22 lakhs; taxable processed food ₹11 lakhs; export of processed food ₹5 lakhs.

Computation of aggregate turnover
Particulars₹
Exempt supplies22,00,000
Taxable supplies11,00,000
Exports5,00,000
Total aggregate turnover38,00,000

Answer: Assam is not a special category State for GST registration threshold purposes (it is one under the Constitution, but for registration limits it follows the general category). As an exclusive goods supplier (not in the excepted specified-goods/excepted-State list), the applicable threshold is ₹40 lakhs. Since aggregate turnover of ₹38 lakhs does not exceed ₹40 lakhs, "Healthy Foods" is not liable to register.

ILLUSTRATION 129 — Inter-State supply of services

Mr. Mehta (Mumbai) provides consultancy services to a client in Bangalore; annual turnover ₹15 lakhs. (i) Is he liable to register? (ii) Would the answer change for inter-State handicraft goods instead of services?

Answer: (i) Sec. 24 generally mandates compulsory registration for inter-State suppliers, but Notification No. 10/2017-IT exempts service providers making inter-State supplies with turnover up to ₹20 lakhs — Mr. Mehta (₹15 lakhs) is not liable to register. (ii) For handicraft goods, Notification No. 32/2017-CT similarly exempts inter-State suppliers with turnover up to ₹20 lakhs, provided they hold a PAN and generate e-way bills — if he complies, he is not liable to register; otherwise compulsory registration applies u/s 24.

ILLUSTRATION 130 — Bank account compliance & automatic suspension

M/s. Alpha Traders was granted GST registration on 1st November 2025 and plans to file its first GSTR-1 for November on 11th December 2025, but has not yet opened a current bank account.

Answer: (1) Under Rule 10A, bank details must be furnished within the earlier of 30 days from grant of registration (1st December 2025) or before filing GSTR-1/IFF (11th December 2025) — so the deadline is 1st December 2025. (2) Under Rule 21A(2A), failure to comply results in suspension of registration (often system-automated), intimated electronically in FORM GST REG-31. (3) The suspension for this specific non-compliance is deemed revoked immediately upon furnishing the bank account details on the portal — no separate revocation application is required in this case.

⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: REGISTRATION THRESHOLD & AGGREGATE TURNOVER COMPUTATION

THE TRAP: assuming (i) ₹40 lakhs is the universal goods threshold everywhere, (ii) every "special category" State (Constitution list) gets the ₹10 lakh limit, and (iii) aggregate turnover for the threshold test = only taxable turnover, so exempt supplies, exports and job-worked-goods-supplied-by-the-principal can be left out.

THE TWIST: the ₹40 lakh enhanced limit applies only to exclusive goods suppliers outside the specified-goods list and outside 10 named States (Illustration 122's pan-masala trader stays at ₹20 lakhs). Only Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura get the ₹10 lakh GST-registration threshold, not the Constitution's full 11-State list (Illustration 128's Assam case). And "aggregate turnover" per Sec. 2(6) is far wider than taxable turnover — it pulls in exempt supplies and exports, while a job-worker's own turnover excludes goods supplied on the principal's account, and same-State/same-registration branch transfers without consideration are excluded altogether (Illustration 124).

1. Under Rule 9A (Grant of Registration Electronically), the "Fast-Track" approval within 3 working days is available only if the applicant's monthly output tax liability towards registered persons (B2B) does not exceed:

(a) ₹1,00,000(b) ₹2,50,000(c) ₹5,00,000(d) ₹10,00,000

Correct: b. Rule 9A sets the eligibility threshold for this fast-track option at a monthly B2B output tax liability not exceeding ₹2,50,000.

2. Which of the following numbers is granted to a person who is not liable to obtain registration but is required to make a payment (e.g. penalty) under the Act?

(a) Temporary Reference Number (TRN)(b) Unique Identity Number (UIN)(c) Temporary Identification Number(d) GSTIN

Correct: c. Per Rule 16A, a "Temporary Identification Number" is distinct from the TRN and is granted by the proper officer to an unregistered person solely to facilitate payments like penalties.

3. A registered person must furnish their bank account details (Rule 10A) on the common portal within:

(a) 45 days from the date of grant of registration(b) 30 days from the date of grant of registration or before filing GSTR-3B, whichever is earlier(c) 30 days from the date of grant of registration or before furnishing details of outward supplies (GSTR-1/IFF), whichever is earlier(d) Before the filing of the first Annual Return

Correct: c. Rule 10A mandates furnishing bank details within 30 days of grant of registration OR before filing GSTR-1/IFF, whichever is earlier.

4. Calculate the "Aggregate Turnover" for Mr. X: Taxable supplies ₹10 lakhs; Exempt supplies ₹5 lakhs; Exports ₹5 lakhs; Inward supplies under reverse charge ₹2 lakhs.

(a) ₹15 Lakhs(b) ₹20 Lakhs(c) ₹22 Lakhs(d) ₹10 Lakhs

Correct: b. Aggregate turnover includes taxable supplies, exempt supplies, and exports; it excludes inward supplies taxed under reverse charge. 10 + 5 + 5 = ₹20 lakhs.

5. Which of the following persons is exempt from compulsory registration u/s 24 even if they make inter-State supplies?

(a) A Casual Taxable Person making taxable supplies(b) An Input Service Distributor(c) A person making inter-State supplies of taxable services with aggregate turnover of ₹15 Lakhs(d) A person required to pay tax under Reverse Charge

Correct: c. While Sec. 24 generally mandates compulsory registration for inter-State suppliers, a specific notification exempts persons making inter-State supplies of taxable services if aggregate turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakhs.

6. If an applicant submits their registration application 45 days after becoming liable to register, the "Effective Date of Registration" will be:

(a) The date on which they became liable to registration(b) The date of submission of the application(c) The date of grant of registration(d) The date of 30 days after liability arose

Correct: c. If the application is submitted after the expiry of 30 days from the date of liability, the effective date is the date of the grant of registration.

7. Registration of a taxpayer can be suspended under Rule 21A if:

(a) They fail to furnish bank account details under Rule 10A(b) There are significant differences between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B(c) There are significant differences between GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B (Input Tax Credit)(d) All of the above

Correct: d. Registration can be suspended for contravention of Rule 10A (bank details) or for significant anomalies/differences in returns (GSTR-1 vs 3B, or inward supply mismatches).

8. A "Casual Taxable Person" must apply for registration at least _____ days prior to the commencement of business and the certificate is valid for _____ days initially.

(a) 5 days; 90 days(b) 7 days; 60 days(c) 30 days; 90 days(d) 5 days; 180 days

Correct: a. A casual taxable person must apply at least 5 days prior to business commencement, and the certificate is valid for 90 days.

9. If a registered person wishes to change their "Principal Place of Business" (a Core Field) within the same State, they must submit an application for amendment within:

(a) 30 days of the change(b) 15 days of the change(c) 7 days of the change(d) No approval is required for this change

Correct: b. For changes in core fields (like Principal Place of Business), the taxpayer must apply for amendment within 15 days of the event.

10. Which State is considered a "Special Category State" for the purpose of the reduced ₹10 lakh registration threshold under GST?

(a) Assam(b) Himachal Pradesh(c) Mizoram(d) Uttarakhand

Correct: c. Only Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura are considered special category States for the specific purpose of the ₹10 lakh GST registration threshold (Assam, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand have the higher general limits).

CONCEPT

5.7 Tax Invoice – Electronic Way Bill ★★★ HIGH

An invoice is a commercial instrument issued by a seller to a buyer — it identifies both trading parties, describes and quantifies the goods/services sold, and shows dates, prices, discounts, and delivery/payment terms. It does not create an agreement; it merely records the terms of one already made. GST Law does not prescribe a fixed format of invoice, but it mandates that certain fields be incorporated in it.

  • Why the tax invoice matters: it evidences the supply of goods/services AND is the document a recipient must possess to avail Input Tax Credit (ITC) — no tax invoice or debit note, no ITC.
  • Link to time of supply: GST is chargeable at the time of supply, and the invoice date is the key indicator of that time (broadly, date of invoice or date of receipt of payment, whichever is earlier). Registered persons supplying goods (other than composition dealers) pay GST at the time of issue of invoice, irrespective of when payment is received.

A. Time of Issue of Tax Invoice — Supply of Goods [Sec. 31(1)]

SituationTax invoice must be issued
Supply involves movement of goodsBefore or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient
Supply does not involve movement of goodsBefore or at the time of delivery of goods or making them available to the recipient
Continuous supply of goods (successive statements of account / successive payments) [Sec. 31(4)]Before or at the time each such statement is issued, or each such payment is received
Goods sent/taken on approval for sale or return, removed before the supply takes place [Sec. 31(7)]Before or at the time of supply, or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier

Taxpoint: the Government, on Council recommendation, may by notification specify categories of goods/supplies for which a tax invoice must be issued within a prescribed time and manner.

B. Time of Issue of Tax Invoice — Supply of Services [Sec. 31(2)]

SituationTime limit for issuance
General casesWithin 30 days from the date of the supply of service (45 days for an insurance/banking company or financial institution, including NBFC)
Supply of services ceases before completionAt the time the supply ceases — invoice issued to the extent of the supply made before cessation
Continuous supply — due date of payment ascertainable from contractOn or before the due date of payment
Continuous supply — due date NOT ascertainable from contractBefore or at the time the supplier receives the payment
Continuous supply — payment linked to completion of an eventOn or before the date of completion of that event
Insurance/banking company or financial institution (incl. NBFC), telecom operator, or notified supplier — supplies between distinct persons (branches) u/s 25Before or at the time of recording in books of account, or before expiry of the quarter during which the supply was made

A person who has obtained — or is required to obtain — more than one registration (in one State/UT or across States/UTs) is treated as a “distinct person” for each such registration [Sec. 25(4)].

Taxpoint: for services too, the Government may by notification specify categories of services for which the tax invoice timeline is prescribed, and may specify that (i) another document is deemed to be a tax invoice, or (ii) a tax invoice may not be issued at all for certain categories.

⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: GOODS vs SERVICES — ONE IS EVENT-BASED, THE OTHER IS TIME-BASED

THE TRAP: students apply the same rule to both — e.g. assuming services also get a "before/at removal" trigger, or that goods get a "30-day window" like services.

THE TWIST: for GOODS the invoice is tied to a physical EVENT — removal (if goods move) or delivery (if they don't). For SERVICES it is tied to a TIME WINDOW from the date of supply — 30 days generally, stretched to 45 days only for insurance/banking companies, financial institutions and NBFCs. There is no 45-day rule for goods, and no "removal" concept for services.

e-Invoice

Turnover > ₹ 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 → e-Invoicing is MANDATORY

Aggregate turnover includes the turnover of ALL GSTINs held under a single PAN across India (i.e., the ₹5 crore test is applied PAN-wide, not GSTIN-wise).

Irrespective of turnover, e-Invoicing does NOT apply (for now, per CBIC Notification No. 13/2020 – CT and related notifications) to:

  • An insurer, a banking company, or a financial institution (including an NBFC)
  • A Goods Transport Agency (GTA)
  • A registered person supplying passenger transportation services
  • A registered person supplying services by way of admission to exhibition of cinematographic films in multiplex screens
  • An SEZ unit (excluded via Notification No. 61/2020 – CT)
  • A government department and local authority (excluded via Notification No. 23/2021 – CT)

An e-Invoice is not required to be issued in multiple copies.

Taxpoint: taxpayers with turnover of ₹ 10 crore and above are restricted from reporting invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) that are older than 30 days from the date of issue.

Other Invoicing Situations

  • Invoice by recipient under Reverse Charge [Rule 47A]: where an invoice must be issued u/s 31(3)(f) by a registered person liable to pay tax u/s 9(3) or 9(4), it must be issued within 30 days from the date of receipt of the supply of goods or services.
  • Consolidated Invoice [Sec. 31(3)(b) & proviso to Rule 46]: a registered person need not issue a tax invoice where the value of goods/services supplied is less than ₹ 200, provided the recipient is unregistered AND does not require an invoice — instead, a consolidated tax invoice is issued for such supplies at the close of each day. (This relaxation does not apply to suppliers of admission-to-cinematograph-films-in-multiplex services.)
  • Revised Invoice after Registration [Sec. 31(3)(a) r.w.r. 53(2)]: a registered person may, within 1 month from the date of issuance of the certificate of registration, issue a revised invoice against invoices already issued during the period from the effective date of registration up to the date of issuance of the certificate. A consolidated revised tax invoice may be issued for all taxable supplies to an unregistered recipient during that period; however, for inter-State supplies where the value does not exceed ₹ 2,50,000, a consolidated revised invoice may be issued separately for all unregistered recipients located in a State.
  • Bill of Supply [Sec. 31(3)(c)]: issued instead of a tax invoice by a registered person supplying exempted goods/services, or paying tax under the composition levy (Sec. 10). The ₹ 200 relaxation (no document needed) applies here too. A composition dealer must mark “composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies” at the top of the bill of supply; a supplier under the concessional-rate Notification No. 2/2019-CT(R) marks a corresponding legend.
  • Receipt Voucher [Sec. 31(3)(d)]: issued on receipt of advance payment for any supply of goods/services.
  • Refund Voucher [Sec. 31(3)(e)]: issued where a receipt voucher was issued for an advance, but subsequently no supply is made and no tax invoice follows — issued to the person who made the payment.
  • Invoice under Reverse Charge [Sec. 31(3)(f)/(g)]: a registered person liable to pay tax u/s 9(3) or 9(4) must issue an invoice (in respect of goods/services received from an unregistered supplier) on the date of receipt, and must issue a payment voucher at the time of making payment to the supplier. Taxpoint: “supplier who is not registered” includes a supplier registered solely for TDS deduction u/s 51.
  • Facility of digital payment [Sec. 31A]: the Government may prescribe a class of registered persons who must offer prescribed electronic-payment modes to recipients. Taxpoint (source's own cross-reference): while Sec. 31A is an enabling GST provision, a parallel mandate exists u/s 269SU of the Income-tax Act, 1961, requiring businesses with turnover > ₹ 50 crore to provide digital payment modes — consistent treatment across Direct and Indirect tax law.
  • Prohibition of unauthorised collection of tax [Sec. 32]: an unregistered person cannot collect any amount as "tax" on a supply; a registered person cannot collect tax except strictly per the Act/Rules.
  • Amount of tax to be indicated [Sec. 33]: where a supply is made for consideration, every person liable to pay tax must prominently indicate, in all assessment/tax-invoice/like documents, the tax amount forming part of the price.

Credit Note and Debit Note [Sec. 34]

 Credit NoteDebit Note
Issued whenTaxable value/tax charged in the tax invoice EXCEEDS the taxable value/tax payable; OR goods are returned by the recipient; OR goods/services supplied are found deficientTaxable value/tax charged in the tax invoice is LESS than the taxable value/tax payable
Issued byThe registered person who supplied the goods/services (to the recipient)The registered person who supplied the goods/services (to the recipient)

Note: “Debit note” includes a supplementary invoice.

Maximum time limit for a credit-note adjustment (reduction of output tax): earlier of — (a) 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or (b) the date of furnishing the relevant annual return.

No reduction in output tax liability is permitted if: (i) the ITC attributable to the credit note, if availed, has not been reversed by the recipient (where the recipient is registered); or (ii) the incidence of tax on that supply has been passed on to any other person (in other cases).

Content of Tax Invoice [Rule 46]

Subject to Rule 54, a tax invoice under Sec. 31 must contain:

  • (a) Name, address and GSTIN of the supplier
  • (b) A consecutive serial number — not exceeding 16 characters, unique for a financial year
  • (c) Date of issue
  • (d) Name, address and GSTIN/UIN of the recipient, if registered
  • (e) Name, address (incl. delivery address, State name and code) of the recipient if UNREGISTERED and the taxable supply value is ₹ 50,000 or more
  • (f) Same details if unregistered and value is under ₹ 50,000, but ONLY if the recipient requests they be recorded
  • (g) HSN (Harmonised System of Nomenclature) code for goods or services
  • (h) Description of goods or services
  • (i) Quantity (for goods) and unit / Unique Quantity Code
  • (j) Total value of supply
  • (k) Taxable value (after discount/abatement, if any)
  • (l) Rate of tax (CGST, SGST, IGST, UTGST or cess)
  • (m) Amount of tax charged
  • (n) Place of supply and State name, for inter-State trade
  • (o) Address of delivery, if different from place of supply
  • (p) Whether tax is payable on reverse charge basis
  • (q) Signature or digital signature of the supplier/authorised representative
  • (r) QR code embedding the Invoice Reference Number (IRN), where an e-invoice has been issued under Rule 48(4)

Taxpoint: for online money gaming, or services supplied through an e-commerce operator, or OIDAR services, to an unregistered recipient — the invoice must state the recipient's State name (deemed the address on record) irrespective of the value of supply.

HSN code digits on invoice — keyed to PRECEDING financial year's turnover

Turnover up to ₹ 5 crore in the preceding FY → 4-digit HSN mandatory, but only for B2B transactions.

Turnover exceeding ₹ 5 crore in the preceding FY → 6-digit HSN mandatory, for ALL transactions (not just B2B).

Further Rule 46 Taxpoints

  • Export/SEZ endorsement: invoices for export of goods/services must carry the endorsement “SUPPLY MEANT FOR EXPORT/SUPPLY TO SEZ UNIT OR SEZ DEVELOPER FOR AUTHORISED OPERATIONS ON PAYMENT OF INTEGRATED TAX” (or the “...UNDER BOND OR LETTER OF UNDERTAKING WITHOUT PAYMENT OF INTEGRATED TAX” variant), and instead of clause (e) details, must show the recipient's name/address, delivery address, and country of destination.
  • Electronic invoice: where issued per the Information Technology Act, 2000, the supplier's signature/digital signature is NOT required.
  • Invoice-cum-bill of supply [Rule 46A]: where a registered person supplies both taxable and exempted goods/services to an unregistered person, a single combined document may be issued.
⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: 4-DIGIT vs 6-DIGIT HSN

THE TRAP: assuming the 6-digit HSN rule applies only to B2B supplies (mirroring the 4-digit rule), or that turnover ₹ 5 crore itself is the crossover figure for both digit-counts identically.

THE TWIST: at turnover up to ₹ 5 crore (preceding FY), 4-digit HSN is mandatory ONLY for B2B invoices. The moment turnover EXCEEDS ₹ 5 crore, the requirement jumps to 6-digit HSN and widens to ALL transactions — B2B and B2C alike.

Manner of Issuing Invoice [Rule 48] and Tax Invoice in Special Cases [Rule 54]

Supply ofCopies preparedMarkings
GoodsTriplicateOriginal – FOR RECIPIENT; Duplicate – FOR TRANSPORTER; Triplicate – FOR SUPPLIER
ServicesDuplicateOriginal – FOR RECIPIENT; Duplicate – FOR SUPPLIER
  • The serial number of invoices issued in a tax period is furnished electronically via Form GSTR-1 or GSTR-1A.
  • e-Invoice mechanism: notified classes of registered persons must prepare invoices per Form GST INV-01, after obtaining an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) by uploading details to the Common GST Electronic Portal. The Commissioner may, by notification, exempt a person/class from e-invoicing for a specified period. An invoice issued by an e-invoicing-covered person in any other manner is NOT treated as a valid invoice.
  • Input Service Distributor [Rule 54(1)]: ISD invoice/credit note must show name/address/GSTIN of the ISD, serial number, date, recipient's GSTIN, amount of credit distributed, and signature.
  • Goods Transport Agency (GTA) [Rule 54(3)]: the document must show gross weight of consignment, name of consignor/consignee, registration number of the goods carriage, details of goods/place of origin/destination, GSTIN of the person liable to pay tax (consignor, consignee, or the GTA), plus the standard Rule 46 particulars.
  • Passenger Transportation Service [Rule 54(4)]: the ticket (in any form, serially numbered or not, with or without the recipient's address) is itself deemed the tax invoice. No signature is required for an electronic ticket issued per the IT Act, 2000.
  • Multiplex cinema admission [Rule 54]: the electronic ticket is deemed a tax invoice for all purposes, even without recipient details. Screens other than multiplex screens may follow the same procedure at the supplier's option.

Electronic Way Bill (E-Way Bill) [Sec. 68; Rules 138 – 138E]

Under Sec. 68, the person in charge of a conveyance carrying a consignment of goods above a specified value must carry the prescribed documents and devices, and produce them for inspection when the conveyance is intercepted by a proper officer.

E-way bill (Form GST EWB-01) is required for movement of goods of consignment value MORE THAN ₹ 50,000

Tested either against each single invoice, or the aggregate of all invoices carried in one vehicle/conveyance.

An e-way bill is an electronic document, available to the consignor (supplier), consignee (recipient), and transporter, generated on the common portal to evidence movement of goods. It has two parts:

  • Part A: GSTIN of supplier and recipient, place of despatch (PIN code), place of delivery (PIN code), document (tax invoice / bill of supply / delivery challan / bill of entry) number and date, value of goods, HSN code, and reasons for transportation.
  • Part B: transport details — transport document number (Goods Receipt Number / Railway Receipt Number / Airway Bill Number / Bill of Lading Number) and vehicle number for road transport.

Rule 138 provides that information must be furnished PRIOR TO the commencement of movement of goods, and the e-way bill requirement applies whether the movement is in relation to a supply or for reasons other than a supply.

Benefits of the e-way bill mechanism: elimination of State-boundary check-posts (physical interface replaced by digital interface); faster movement of goods; improved truck turnaround time (helping the logistics industry via longer average distances, lower travel time and cost); and greater transparency, since the consignor must also give consignee details.

When Should an E-Way Bill Be Generated?

An e-way bill is generated for movement of goods in a vehicle/conveyance of value more than ₹ 50,000 (per invoice, or in aggregate of all invoices in that vehicle), when the movement is:

  • In relation to a ‘supply’
  • For reasons OTHER than a supply (e.g. a return)
  • Due to an inward supply from an unregistered person

A ‘supply’ here may be: (a) for consideration in the course of business; (b) for consideration but NOT in the course of business; or (c) without consideration at all. In everyday terms, this covers Sale, Transfer (e.g. branch transfers), and Barter/Exchange (payment in goods, not money).

Mandatory even BELOW ₹ 50,000 for these two categories of goods:

  • Inter-State movement of goods by/to the Principal from/to a Job-worker (Principal to registered job-worker, or vice versa)
  • Inter-State transport of Handicraft goods by a dealer who is exempted from GST registration
⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: THE ₹50,000 E-WAY BILL THRESHOLD ISN'T ABSOLUTE

THE TRAP: assuming that consignments valued ₹ 50,000 or below NEVER need an e-way bill, and that the threshold is a flat, universal cut-off with no carve-outs either way.

THE TWIST: two named exceptions REQUIRE an e-way bill even below ₹ 50,000 — inter-State movement to/from a job-worker, and inter-State transport of handicraft goods by a registration-exempt dealer. Conversely, a registered person or transporter MAY voluntarily generate one below ₹ 50,000 even where not compulsory. And for the specific Annexure list of goods that are otherwise EWB-exempt (Rule 138F), if the value of supply exceeds ₹ 2,00,000, Part A of Form GST EWB-01 must still be furnished before movement begins.

Who Should Generate an E-Way Bill?

WhoWhenWhat is filled
Every registered person under GSTBefore movement of goodsFills Part A — Form GST EWB-01
Registered person is consignor or consignee (transport owned or hired), or is the recipient of goodsBefore movement of goodsFills Part B — Form GST EWB-01
Registered person is consignor/consignee and hands the goods to a transporterBefore movement of goodsRegistered person fills Part A; furnishes transporter information for Part B of Form GST EWB-01
Transporter of goodsBefore movement of goodsGenerates the e-way bill based on information the registered person shared in Part A
Unregistered person under GST, where the recipient is registeredCompliance done by the recipient, as if it were the supplier(i) If goods move ≤ 50 km within the same State/UT from the consignor's place of business to the transporter's place for further transport, Part B (conveyance details) may be skipped. (ii) If supply is by air, ship or railways, Part A is filled by the consignor or the recipient.
  • Where a transporter carries multiple consignments in a single conveyance, they may use Form GST EWB-02 to produce a consolidated e-way bill, citing the e-way bill numbers of each consignment.
  • If neither consignor nor consignee has generated an e-way bill, the transporter may do so by filling Part A of Form GST EWB-01, based on the invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan handed to them.
  • Unregistered transporters are issued a Transporter ID upon enrolling on the e-way bill portal, after which they too can generate e-way bills.

When an E-Way Bill Is NOT Required

  • (a) Goods specified in the Annexure list (Subject to Rule 138F) — LPG for household/NDEC customers; Kerosene oil sold under PDS; Postal baggage transported by the Department of Posts; natural/cultured pearls, precious/semi-precious stones, precious metals and metal-clad-with-precious-metal (Chapter 71); jewellery, goldsmiths'/silversmiths' wares and other articles (Chapter 71); Currency; used personal and household effects; unworked coral (0508) and worked coral (9601)
  • (b) Goods transported by a Non-motorised conveyance
  • (c) Goods transported from customs port/airport/air cargo complex/land customs station to an inland container depot or container freight station for Customs clearance
  • (d) Movement of goods within areas notified under Rule 138(14)(d) of the State/UT GST Rules for that State/UT
  • (e) Goods (other than de-oiled cake) specified in the Schedule to Notification No. 2/2017-Central Tax (Rate)
  • (f) Alcoholic liquor for human consumption, petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, or aviation turbine fuel
  • (g) Supply treated as "No Supply" under Schedule III of the Act
  • (h) Goods moved under customs bond (ICD/CFS to customs port etc., or between customs stations), or under customs supervision/seal
  • (i) Transit cargo from or to Nepal or Bhutan
  • (j) Goods exempt from tax under Notification No. 7/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and Notification No. 26/2017-Central Tax (Rate)
  • (k) Movement caused by a defence formation under the Ministry of Defence, as consignor or consignee
  • (l) Consignor is the Central Government, a State Government, or a local authority, for transport by rail
  • (m) Empty cargo containers being transported
  • (n) Goods transported up to 20 km from the consignor's place of business to a weighbridge (and back), accompanied by a delivery challan under Rule 55
  • (o) Empty cylinders for packing LPG, moved for reasons other than supply

Taxpoint: Part B of the e-way bill need not be filled where the distance between the consignor/consignee and the transporter is less than 50 km and transport is within the same State.

Validity of E-Way Bill

Validity is calculated from the date and time of generation of the e-way bill, based on distance travelled:

Type of ConveyanceDistanceValidity
Other than Over Dimensional CargoLess than 200 km1 Day
Other than Over Dimensional CargoFor every additional 200 km or part thereofAdditional 1 Day
Over Dimensional CargoLess than 20 km1 Day
Over Dimensional CargoFor every additional 20 km or part thereofAdditional 1 Day

Documents to Generate an E-Way Bill; Bill-To/Ship-To; Cancellation

  • Documents/details needed: Invoice / Bill of Supply / Challan relating to the consignment; for road transport — Transporter ID or Vehicle number; for rail/air/ship — Transporter ID, Transport document number, and date on the document.
  • Bill To–Ship To: where the taxpayer bills to one party but sends the consignment to another party as per business requirements, the e-way bill system has a ‘Bill To’ and ‘Ship To’ provision to handle it.
  • Bill From–Dispatch From: where the supplier bills from its business premises to the consignee but moves the consignment from a different (other) premises, this is termed ‘Billing From’ and ‘Dispatching From.’
  • Cancellation: an e-way bill once generated cannot be DELETED, but CAN be cancelled by the generator within 24 hours of generation — unless it has already been verified by a proper officer, in which case it cannot be cancelled. Grounds for cancellation: goods are not transported, or not transported as per the details furnished.

Taxpoint: generation, cancellation, updation and assignment of the e-way bill are all also made available via SMS to the supplier, recipient, and transporter.

Documents/Devices to be Carried, Verification and Inspection [Rules 138A – 138D]

  • Rule 138A — documents/devices carried: the person in charge of a conveyance must carry (a) the invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan, and (b) a physical copy of the e-way bill, or its number in electronic form, or a number mapped to an RFID device on the conveyance (as notified by the Commissioner) — except that (b) does not apply to movement by rail, air, or vessel. For imported goods, a copy of the Bill of Entry must also be carried, with its number and date shown in Part A of Form GST EWB-01. Where an invoice is issued per Rule 48(4), the QR code with embedded IRN may be produced electronically instead of the physical tax invoice. The Commissioner may notify a class of transporters to obtain and embed an RFID device and map the e-way bill to it before movement; and where circumstances warrant, may require the person-in-charge to instead carry the tax invoice/bill of supply/bill of entry, or a delivery challan (for movement other than by way of supply).
  • Rule 138B — verification of documents and conveyances: the Commissioner (or an officer empowered by him) may authorise a proper officer to intercept any conveyance to verify the e-way bill (physical or electronic) for inter-State and intra-State movement. RFID readers are to be installed at verification points; verification of movement is done through such readers where the e-way bill is mapped to the device. Physical verification of conveyances is otherwise carried out by an authorised proper officer, and on specific evasion information, by another officer with the Commissioner's approval.
  • Rule 138C — inspection and verification of goods: a summary report of every in-transit inspection is recorded online in Part A of Form GST EWB-03 within 24 hours of inspection; the final report goes in Part B of Form GST EWB-03 within 3 days of inspection (extendable by a further period not exceeding 3 days, for sufficient cause). Both periods run from the midnight of the date the vehicle was intercepted. Once a conveyance has been physically verified in transit anywhere in India, no further physical verification of that conveyance is done again (in that State/UT) unless specific new evasion information surfaces.
  • Rule 138D — detention of vehicle: where a vehicle is intercepted and detained for more than 30 minutes, the transporter may upload that information in Form GST EWB-04 on the common portal.
⚠ TRAP

⚠ TRAP: DON'T MIX UP THE SEVEN DIFFERENT RUPEE THRESHOLDS IN THIS TOPIC

THE TRAP: the topic packs several different threshold figures close together, and exam options are designed to swap them — e.g. answering ₹200 where ₹50,000 is meant, or vice-versa.

THE TWIST: keep them separate by what each one gates — ₹200 = value below which NO tax invoice/bill of supply is compulsorily needed for an unregistered, non-requesting recipient (consolidated invoice at day's close instead). ₹50,000 = value at/above which an unregistered recipient's name/address must appear on the tax invoice [Rule 46(e)], AND also the E-Way Bill trigger value [Rule 138]. ₹2,50,000 = the inter-State cap for issuing a separate consolidated REVISED invoice to unregistered recipients in a State [Rule 53(2)]. ₹2,00,000 = the value above which Part A of the e-way bill is still required even for the Rule 138F Annexure-exempt goods list. ₹5 crore = the e-invoicing turnover threshold (also the HSN 4-digit/6-digit crossover). ₹10 crore = the turnover above which e-invoices cannot be reported to the IRP more than 30 days late.

Practice Problems / Quick MCQ (from the source)

1. A registered person supplying taxable goods must issue a tax invoice when the supply involves the movement of goods:

(a) At the time of delivery to the recipient.(b) Before or at the time of removal of goods for supply.(c) Within 30 days of removal.(d) At the close of the financial year.

2. What is the time limit for issuing a tax invoice for the supply of taxable services in general cases?

(a) Within 45 days from the date of supply.(b) Before the expiry of the quarter.(c) Within 30 days from the date of the supply of service.(d) At the time of receipt of payment only.

3. Under Rule 47A, if a registered person is liable to pay tax under Reverse Charge (RCM), they must issue an invoice within:

(a) 15 days from the date of receipt of supply.(b) 30 days from the date of receipt of supply.(c) 45 days from the date of receipt of supply.(d) The same day the supply is received.

4. A registered person is not required to issue a tax invoice if the value of goods/services supplied is less than ₹ 200, provided:

(a) The recipient is a registered person.(b) The recipient is unregistered and does not require such an invoice.(c) The supply is an inter-state supply.(d) The supplier is a multiplex.

5. For taxpayers with an aggregate turnover exceeding ₹ 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18, which of the following is mandatory?

(a) Bill of Supply for all B2B transactions.(b) E-invoicing.(c) Receipt Voucher for all sales.(d) 8-digit HSN code for all products.

6. Which document is issued when a registered person receives an advance payment for a supply of services?

(a) Tax Invoice.(b) Payment Voucher.(c) Receipt Voucher.(d) Refund Voucher.

7. If a registered person's turnover in the preceding financial year was ₹ 10 crore, how many digits of the HSN code must they mention on their invoices?

(a) 2 digits.(b) 4 digits.(c) 6 digits.(d) 8 digits.

8. An E-way bill is mandatorily required for the movement of goods of consignment value exceeding:

(a) ₹ 10,000.(b) ₹ 20,000.(c) ₹ 50,000.(d) ₹ 1,00,000.

9. What is the validity of an E-way bill for a distance of 150 km for cargo other than "Over Dimensional Cargo"?

(a) 1 day.(b) 2 days.(c) 5 days.(d) 15 days.

10. In the case of an "Invoice-cum-bill of supply," it can be issued when:

(a) A registered person supplies taxable goods to another registered person.(b) A registered person supplies taxable as well as exempted goods to an unregistered person.(c) A composition dealer supplies goods to a registered person.(d) An unregistered person supplies goods to a registered person.
QCorrectReason
1(b)Sec. 31(1) — where supply involves movement of goods, invoice is issued before or at the time of removal for supply to the recipient.
2(c)General provision for supply of services: invoice within 30 days from the date of supply of service.
3(b)Rule 47A mandates a recipient liable under RCM to issue the invoice within 30 days from date of receipt of goods/services.
4(b)Sec. 31(3)(b) allows non-issuance of a tax invoice for values under ₹ 200 if the recipient is unregistered and does not require the invoice.
5(b)Taxpayers must comply with e-invoicing once turnover exceeds ₹ 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards.
6(c)Sec. 31(3)(d) — a registered person issues a receipt voucher evidencing receipt of advance payment.
7(c)Where turnover exceeds ₹ 5 crore in the preceding financial year, a 6-digit HSN code is required on invoices for all transactions.
8(c)Rule 138 — an e-way bill is generated for movement of goods where the consignment value exceeds ₹ 50,000.
9(a)For conveyances other than over-dimensional cargo, validity is 1 day for a distance of less than 200 km.
10(b)Rule 46A allows a single "invoice-cum-bill of supply" when a registered person supplies both taxable and exempted goods/services to an unregistered person.
CONCEPT

5.8 Returns and Payment of Taxes ★★★ HIGH

The return mechanism under GST rests on electronic filing, uploading of invoice-level information, auto-population of Input Tax Credit from the supplier's return into the recipient's return, invoice-level matching, and auto-reversal of ITC on mismatch. A return serves five purposes: (a) a mode for transferring information to the tax administration; (b) a compliance-verification tool; (c) finalisation of tax liability within the period of limitation; (d) inputs for policy decisions; and (e) management of audit and anti-evasion programmes.

A regular taxpayer furnishes monthly returns plus one annual return. Separate return forms exist for a composition taxpayer, a non-resident taxpayer, an Input Service Distributor, a person liable to deduct/collect tax (TDS/TCS), and a person granted a Unique Identification Number (UIN) — no taxpayer files every return type; each files only the forms its activities require. Returns are filed online, through the GSTN portal (www.gst.gov.in), GSTN offline utilities, or GST Suvidha Providers (GSPs).
