10(c)Where more than one transaction value of identical goods is found, the lowest of such values shall be used for determining the value of imported goods.
22 EXAM FACTS — CUSTOMS ACT & RULES (Module 6)

① Entry 83 of List I, Schedule VII empowers the Union to levy duties on imports and exports; the Customs Act, 1962 is effective from 1-2-1963 and Sec. 12 is its charging section. Rates come from the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 — First Schedule = import duty, Second Schedule = export duty. Duty is on the GOODS, not on the person.

② Territorial waters = 12 nautical miles from the baseline (and “India” includes them). Indian Customs Waters u/s 2(28), the EEZ and the Continental Shelf all run to 200 nautical miles. 1 nautical mile = 1.1515 miles = 1.852 km.

③ Taxable event: import commences on crossing territorial waters and completes when the goods mix with the mass of goods in India; for home consumption it is when the goods reach the customs barriers and the bill of entry for home consumption is filed; for warehoused goods, import takes place on clearance for home consumption. Export is complete only when goods cross the territorial waters — goods sinking within them are not exported.

④ Sec. 13 (pilferage after unloading, before the clearance order, not re-stored) → no duty; but duty revives if goods are re-stored, and Sec. 13 does not apply to goods pilfered after warehousing. Sec. 23(1) (total loss or destruction before clearance) → remission, burden on the importer, and it DOES cover warehoused goods. Where Sec. 13 applies, Sec. 23(1) does not.

⑤ Sec. 22 abatement: Duty on damaged goods = (Value of damaged goods ÷ Value before damage) × Duty before damage. Source example: ₹10,000 × ₹40,000 ÷ ₹1,00,000 = ₹4,000. The damaged value may be fixed by the proper officer OR by public auction/tender — at the owner's option.

⑥ Sec. 23(2): relinquishment of title must be unconditional and made before the order for clearance for home consumption or for deposit in a warehouse — and is not allowed where an offence appears to have been committed.

⑦ Sec. 19: a set of articles liable at different ad valorem rates is chargeable at the HIGHEST of those rates (Illustration 3: a ₹5,000 grooming kit containing Nil/10%/20%/30% items is taxed wholly at 30%). Accessories, spare parts and repair implements take the same rate as the main article. Sec. 20: goods exported for repairs and re-imported are taxed only on fair cost of repairs + insurance and freight both ways, provided ownership has not changed.

⑧ Sec. 25: duty is not collected where the amount leviable does not exceed ₹100; an exemption is valid up to the 31st March falling immediately after 2 years from the date of grant or variation.

⑨ Tariff classification: First Schedule has 21 Sections and 98 Chapters on the HSN (WCO, 137+ countries). 4-digit = heading, 6-digit = sub-heading, 8-digit = Tariff Item.

⑩ Social Welfare Surcharge = 10% of total customs duties (3% for gold/silver, incl. platinum-plated, unwrought, semi-manufactured or powder), on imports only — never on export. Six items are EXCLUDED from its base: Safeguard Duty, CVD on subsidized article, Anti-dumping duty, IGST, GST Compensation Cess, AIDC.

⑪ IGST on imports is levied by Sec. 3(7) and GST Compensation Cess by Sec. 3(9) of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975. Both use the SAME base — Sec. 14 value + BCD + any sum chargeable like a duty of customs — and both exclude the IGST and the cess from that base. The cess is extended up to 31-03-2026. ITC of both is available under GST law.

⑫ Safeguard measures [Sec. 8B] answer increased quantities causing serious injury: provisional measures max 200 days; duty lapses after 4 years, extendable to 10 years; not imposed where a developing country's share is ≤ 3%, or all such countries together ≤ 9%, of total imports of that article.

⑬ Countervailing duty [Sec. 9] answers a subsidy and cannot exceed the subsidy amount. Anti-dumping duty [Sec. 9A] answers dumping and cannot exceed the Margin of Dumping = Normal Value − Export Price. Both run 5 years, extendable by 5, with a 1-year pending-review extension, and both may be levied retrospectively but not beyond 90 days from the notification. Sec. 9B bars both duties on the same situation of dumping or export subsidization.

⑭ Sec. 14(1) transaction value requires: price actually paid or payable · sold for export to/from India · delivery at the time and place of importation/exportation · buyer and seller not related · price the sole consideration. Sec. 14(2) tariff value fixed by CBIC (crude palm oil, crude palmolein, crude soyabean oil, brass scrap, poppy seeds) overrides it where fixed.

⑮ Import valuation hierarchy: Rule 3 (transaction) → Rule 4 (identical) → Rule 5 (similar) → Rule 7 (deductive) → Rule 8 (computed) → Rule 9 (residual). Only Rules 7 and 8 may be swapped, at the importer's request. Where more than one transaction value of identical or similar goods exists, take the LOWEST. Rule 12 is a rejection mechanism, not a valuation method — after rejection, proceed sequentially through Rules 4 to 9.

⑯ Related persons include anyone owning, controlling or holding 5% or more of the voting rights of both, plus officers/directors of one another's businesses, partners, employer-employee, one controlling the other, both controlled by a third, together controlling a third, and members of the same family. A related-party price is still accepted if the relationship did not influence it, or it closely approximates an identical/similar-goods transaction, deductive or computed test value.

⑰ Freight: actual; if unascertained 20% of FOB; by AIR always capped at 20% of FOB even when the actual is known. Insurance: actual; if unascertained 1.125% of FOB. From a CIF figure: transport = CIF × 20/120, insurance = CIF × 1.125/101.125.

⑱ ADDED to value: commission and brokerage (not buying commission), containers, packing, buyer's free-issue materials/tools/dies/moulds, foreign engineering and design work, royalties and licence fees payable as a condition of sale, resale proceeds accruing to the seller, ship demurrage on chartered vessels and lighterage/barge charges. NOT added: buying commission, durable and returnable packing, Indian design/development work, Indian duties and taxes, port-to-factory transport and insurance, erection charges in India, unloading/landing charges at the place of importation and port demurrage for delay in clearing.

⑲ Rule 7 deductive value uses the unit price in the greatest aggregate quantity to UNRELATED persons — group sales by price, total the units at each price, and ignore sales made after 90 days from importation. Then remember the residue is Assessable Value PLUS duty: at 25%, ₹98 − ₹18 = ₹80 = 125% of AV, so AV = ₹64 per unit.

⑳ Sec. 15: rate of duty and tariff valuation follow the bill-of-entry date — but a bill of entry presented BEFORE entry inwards / arrival is deemed presented on that later date for the rate of duty. The exchange rate, however, is always that in force on the ACTUAL date of presentation, and always the CBIC rate (selling for import, buying for export) — RBI and inter-bank rates are distractors. Sec. 16: for exports the relevant date is the date of the order permitting clearance and loading u/s 51. Neither section applies to baggage or goods imported by post.

㉑ The duty ladder, in order and on the right base: [A] Assessable Value (CIF) → [B] BCD = rate × A → [C] SWS = 10% of B → [D] Value for IGST = A + B + C → [E] IGST = 18% × D → [F] Cess = rate × D → Total duty payable = B + C + E + F. Shortcut used by the source: BCD 12% + SWS = an effective 13.20% on assessable value.

㉒ Export valuation runs a shorter ladder — Rule 3 (transaction value, accepted even between related parties if the relationship did not influence the price) → Rule 4 (comparison with goods of like kind and quality) → Rule 5 (computed value) → Rule 6 (residual, where local market price may not be the ONLY basis). The Export Goods Valuation Rules, 2007 came into force on 10th October, 2007, generally FOB is the price, and no Social Welfare Surcharge is levied on export.

MODULE 6 CLOSING DRILL (retrieval practice — do not skip, ~10 minutes): put this document down and, on rough paper, write from memory: (1) the charging section of the Customs Act and the two Schedules of the Customs Tariff Act, with the maritime distances for territorial waters versus Indian Customs Waters u/s 2(28); (2) the taxable event for imports cleared for home consumption, for warehoused goods, and for exports; (3) the four relief provisions — Sec. 13, 22, 23(1) and 23(2) — with what triggers each and the Sec. 22 proportion formula; (4) every duty in the stack with its charging Section and the base it is computed ON: BCD, SWS (including the six exclusions and the 3% gold/silver rate), IGST u/s 3(7), Compensation Cess u/s 3(9), AIDC, Safeguard u/s 8B, CVD u/s 9, Anti-dumping u/s 9A; (5) the durations — 200 days, 4 years, 10 years, 5 years, 90 days — and which duty each belongs to; (6) the six-rung import valuation hierarchy with rule numbers, the one reversible pair, and the “lowest value” rule for identical/similar goods; (7) the full FOB → CIF ladder, including what IS added (lighterage, foreign design, condition-of-sale royalties, free-issue materials) and what is NOT (buying commission, Indian design work, landing charges, port demurrage); (8) the freight and insurance percentages — 20%, 1.125%, the air cap, and the two CIF back-out fractions; (9) the Rule 7 greatest-aggregate-quantity method with its 90-day cut-off and the gross-down for duty; (10) the Sec. 15 deeming rule, and why the exchange-rate date can differ from the duty-rate date; and finally (11) the complete duty ladder A → B → C → D → E → F, then reproduce Illustration 21 end to end from the raw Yen figures to ₹2,06,374. Check against the notes only after finishing — answering from memory is what converts today's reading into exam-day marks. Anything you could not retrieve, star it and re-attempt tomorrow morning.
The Final Ladder — Every Section, Rate and Formula in Paper 7

One climb through all six modules, Sections and formulas only. Read this straight through the morning of the exam — not to learn anything new, only to fire the recall pathway for what you already know. This paper is decided by whether the right Section number, the right rate and the right base arrive together; everything below is arranged so that they do.

Section A · Direct Taxation (50%) — Module 1: Basics of Income Tax Act (10%)

TopicThe Ladder
1.1 Charge, persons & headsSec. 4 (charging section): income of the PREVIOUS year is charged in the immediately following ASSESSMENT year, at the rate the annual Finance Act fixes for that A.Y. (some incomes carry a rate fixed in the Act itself, e.g. lottery @30% u/s 115BB). Liability arises at the CLOSE of the P.Y.; only quantification is postponed · Constitutional root: Union List Entry 82 (income other than agricultural income), State List Entry 46 (agricultural income) · Person [Sec. 2(31)] — 7 categories: Individual, HUF, Company, Firm (includes LLP), AOP/BOI, Local authority, Artificial juridical person · Income [Sec. 2(24)] is an INCLUSIVE definition — cash and kind, negative income (loss), embezzled money; pin money and mere reimbursement are never income · Five heads [Sec. 14]: Salaries · House Property · Profits and Gains of Business or Profession · Capital Gains · Other Sources (residual) · Total Income [Sec. 2(45) r/w 80A(1)] = Gross Total Income − Chapter VIA deductions (80C to 80U) · Rounding: Total Income to nearest ₹10 [Sec. 288A, paise ignored, ₹5 rounds up]; tax, TDS, advance tax, interest, penalty and refund to nearest ₹10 [Sec. 288B] · Capital receipt: NOT taxable unless the Act says so. Revenue receipt: taxable UNLESS the Act exempts it — lump sum vs. instalment, and value enhancement by a TENANT, never flip the classification · Diversion of income (obligation intercepts BEFORE the assessee) → not taxable; Application of income (obligation discharged AFTER income reaches him) → taxable.
1.2 Residential status & incidenceSec. 6(1) — Resident, ALTERNATIVE tests: (a) 182 days or more in the P.Y. [6(1)(a)]; OR (c) 60 days in the P.Y. + 365 days or more in the preceding 4 P.Y.s [6(1)(c)]. For an Indian citizen leaving India for employment or as a ship's crew member, 6(1)(c) drops out entirely — only the 182-day test can make him resident. Both the date of arrival and the date of departure count as days in India. Rule 126: for an Indian-citizen crew member on an "eligible voyage," the period between the Continuous Discharge Certificate's joining and signing-off dates is EXCLUDED · Sec. 6(6) — Ordinarily Resident, runs ONLY after Resident is established, and needs BOTH: (a) resident in at least 2 of the 10 preceding P.Y.s; AND (b) 730 days or more present in the 7 preceding P.Y.s. Failing either → Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident · Sec. 6(3): an Indian company is ALWAYS resident; a foreign company is resident only if its Place of Effective Management for that year is in India. No ROR/RNOR split for companies, firms, AOPs or BOIs · Sec. 5 — incidence: income accrued OR received in India is taxable for everyone; foreign business/profession income (controlled or set up outside India) is taxable for ROR only; income already received or accrued abroad in an earlier year stays untaxed for all three categories even if remitted later.
1.3 Agricultural incomeSec. 2(1A): income must be DERIVED FROM LAND in India by agricultural operations — poultry, dairy, fisheries and livestock income fail this test even on a farm; interest on a mortgage of agricultural land or on arrears of its rent is a return on money, not land · A Basic Operation (human skill and labour applied to land BEFORE germination — tilling, sowing, planting, irrigation) qualifies on its own; a Subsequent Operation alone does not; spontaneous growth with no human effort never qualifies · Partial integration applies only where (1) the assessee is an Individual/HUF/AOP/BOI/AJP, (2) non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit, and (3) agricultural income exceeds ₹5,000 — it taxes non-agricultural income at the higher slab rate agricultural income pushes it into · Partly-agricultural splits: Rule 8 tea 60:40 · Rule 7A rubber 65:35 · Rule 7B(1) cured coffee 75:25 · Rule 7B(1A) roasted & ground coffee 60:40.
1.4 Sec. 10 exemptionsA Sec. 10 exemption never enters the computation at all; a Chapter VIA deduction enters GTI and is then subtracted — two different mechanisms · Sec. 14A: no deduction for expenditure incurred to earn income that does not form part of total income, even if that income has not yet accrued or been received · Sec. 10(10D) life-insurance sums wholly exempt (including bonus), EXCEPT sums u/s 80DD(3)/80DDA(3), Keyman policies, and policies issued on/after 1-4-2012 where premium in any year exceeds 10% of the actual capital sum assured (15% for a disabled/specified-disease insured, policies from 1-4-2013) · Sec. 10AA SEZ deduction = Profits of the SEZ undertaking × (Export turnover ÷ Total turnover of the undertaking) — NOT available under the default tax regime.
The Master Ladder — Gross Total Income to Tax Payable (Individual)
Step — Particulars₹
1. Determine residential status [Sec. 6] — it fixes the scope of total income u/s 5—
2. Income from Salaries [Sec. 15–17, less Sec. 16]***
3. Income from House Property [Sec. 22–27]***
4. Profits and Gains of Business or Profession [Sec. 28–44]***
5. Capital Gains [Sec. 45–55A]***
6. Income from Other Sources [Sec. 56–59]***
7. Add: income clubbed u/s 60–65; then set off and carry forward losses [Sec. 70, 71, 71B–74A, 32(2)]***
= GROSS TOTAL INCOME****
8. Less: Deductions under Chapter VI-A [Sec. 80C to 80U], as available in the regime opted(***)
= TOTAL INCOME — rounded to the nearest ₹10 [Sec. 288A]****
9. Tax on Total Income at the slab / special rates for the A.Y.***
10. Less: Rebate u/s 87A (resident individual only; slab-rate tax only)(***)
11. Add: Surcharge (with marginal relief), then Health & Education Cess @ 4%***
12. Less: Relief u/s 89, TDS, TCS, advance tax — balance rounded to nearest ₹10 [Sec. 288B](***)
= TAX PAYABLE / REFUNDABLE****
Rate blockThe figures
Default regime slabs [Sec. 115BAC(1A)]Individual / HUF / AOP (other than co-operative society) / BOI / AJP — all ages, same ₹4,00,000 basic exemption. Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil · ₹4,00,001–8,00,000 5% · ₹8,00,001–12,00,000 10% · ₹12,00,001–16,00,000 15% · ₹16,00,001–20,00,000 20% · ₹20,00,001–24,00,000 25% · above ₹24,00,000 30% · Rebate u/s 87A: resident individual with Total Income not exceeding ₹12,00,000 — lower of 100% of tax or ₹60,000; marginal relief runs up to ₹12,70,587, Marginal Relief = positive value of [Tax on Income − (Income − ₹12,00,000)] · Surcharge: Nil up to ₹50 lakh · 10% ₹50L–1cr · 15% ₹1–2cr · 25% above ₹2cr · Cess 4%.
Old regime slabsSuper senior (resident, age ≥80): up to ₹5,00,000 Nil · ₹5,00,001–10,00,000 20% of excess · above ₹10,00,000 ₹1,00,000 + 30% · Senior (resident, age ≥60): up to ₹3,00,000 Nil · ₹3,00,001–5,00,000 5% · ₹5,00,001–10,00,000 ₹10,000 + 20% · above ₹10,00,000 ₹1,10,000 + 30% · Other individual / HUF / AOP / BOI / AJP: up to ₹2,50,000 Nil · ₹2,50,001–5,00,000 5% · ₹5,00,001–10,00,000 ₹12,500 + 20% · above ₹10,00,000 ₹1,12,500 + 30% · Rebate u/s 87A: resident individual with Total Income not exceeding ₹5,00,000 — lower of 100% of tax or ₹12,500; not available on Sec. 112A gains · Surcharge: Nil / 10% / 15% / 25% / 37% at ₹50L, ₹1cr, ₹2cr and ₹5cr — capped at 15% on dividend and Sec. 111A/112/112A gains, and for an AOP of companies only · Cess 4%.
Non-individual ratesFirm / LLP 30% flat, surcharge 12% if Total Income exceeds ₹1 crore · Domestic company with turnover/gross receipts in P.Y. 2023-24 up to ₹400 crore — 25%; any other domestic company — 30%; surcharge 7% (₹1–10cr) / 12% (above ₹10cr) · Foreign company 35%, surcharge 2% (₹1–10cr) / 5% (above ₹10cr) · Marginal relief is available at every surcharge threshold; Health & Education Cess 4% for all assessees.
A person born on 1st April is treated as attaining that age on 31st March, the day BEFORE the birthday [Circular No. 28/2016] — so a 60th birthday on 1-4-2026 means age 60 is attained in P.Y. 2025-26.

Module 2: Heads of Income (25%) — 2.1 Salaries

RuleThe formula, exactly
Basis of charge [Sec. 15]Salary is taxed on "DUE" basis or "RECEIPT" basis — whichever is EARLIER. The employee's own method of accounting is irrelevant. Advance salary is taxable u/s 17(1)(e) in the year received; an "advance against salary" is a loan and is not taxable under this head at all. Arrear salary is taxed on receipt, with relief u/s 89 available. Foregoing salary already earned is an application of income, not an exemption.
Gratuity [Sec. 10(10)]Covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act [10(10)(ii)] — exempt = MINIMUM of (1) actual gratuity received, (2) ₹20,00,000, (3) (15 ÷ 26) × completed years of service × salary p.m. Fraction in excess of 6 months = a full year · Not covered by the Act [10(10)(iii)] — exempt = LOWER of (1) actual gratuity, (2) ₹20,00,000, (3) ½ × completed years of service × average salary p.m. Any fraction of a year is ignored; the 10-month average runs over the 10 months PRECEDING the month of retirement.
Leave encashment [Sec. 10(10AA)(ii)]Non-Government employee — exempt = MINIMUM of the four: (a) actual leave salary received; (b) ₹25,00,000; (c) 10 × average salary p.m.; (d) [{(1 × completed years of service) − leave actually taken in months} × average salary p.m.] — a maximum of 30 days (one month) average salary for every completed year of service. Here the 10 months END on the date of retirement, not on the month before it.
Pension [Sec. 10(10A)]Uncommuted pension — fully taxable for every employee · Commuted, Government employee (includes local authority and statutory corporation employees, and High Court/Supreme Court Judges) — fully exempt u/s 10(10A)(i) · Commuted, other employee ALSO receiving gratuity — one-third of the total pension he is normally entitled to commute is exempt · Commuted, other employee NOT receiving gratuity — one-half of that total. The fraction always applies to the grossed-up 100% commutation value, never to the sum actually received. Pension to a widow or legal heir is taxable u/s 56, not as salary.
Retrenchment & VRSSec. 10(10B): exempt = MINIMUM of (a) actual compensation, (b) ₹5,00,000, (c) the Sec. 25F(b) Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 amount — 15 days' average pay for every completed year of service or part in excess of 6 months · Sec. 10(10C): exempt = MINIMUM of (a) actual amount received per the guidelines, or (b) ₹5,00,000.
House Rent Allowance [Sec. 10(13A), Rule 2A]Exempt = MINIMUM of the three limbs — (a) actual HRA received; (b) 50% of salary if the HOUSE is in a metro city, 40% of salary otherwise, for the relevant period; (c) rent paid − 10% of salary. "Salary" = Basic + D.A. (only where it forms part of retirement benefits) + commission as a fixed percentage of turnover. Nothing is exempt if the employee lives in his own house or pays no rent. Available only under the OLD regime. Recompute limb by limb whenever salary, rent, city or the fact of renting changes mid-year.
Allowances [Sec. 10(14)]Sec. 10(14)(i) — exempt = MINIMUM of actual amount received or actual expenditure incurred for that purpose · Children education allowance — ₹100 p.m. per child, maximum two children (old regime only) · Children hostel allowance — ₹300 p.m. per child, maximum two children (old regime only) · Truck driver's allowance — minimum of 70% of the allowance or ₹10,000 p.m. (old regime only) · Transport allowance — ₹3,200 p.m., available under BOTH regimes, but only to a blind / deaf and dumb / orthopaedically handicapped employee.
Rent-free accommodationEmployer-OWNED: 10% of salary where the city's population exceeds 40 lakh (2011 census), 7.5% where it exceeds 15 lakh but not 40 lakh, 5% for any other city — charged only for the period the employee OCCUPIED the accommodation · NOT owned by the employer: rent paid or payable by the employer OR 10% of salary, whichever is LOWER, regardless of population · Hotel accommodation: MINIMUM of 24% of salary for the period, or the actual hotel charges, less any rent recovered from the employee · Same accommodation, same employee, later year — value capped at [first-year amount × (CII of the current P.Y. ÷ CII of the P.Y. the accommodation was first provided)] · Furnished accommodation = value of accommodation + value of furniture.
Other perquisites [Sec. 17(2)]Specified employee test: the ₹4,00,000 monetary-salary figure is computed after EXCLUDING all non-monetary benefits, non-taxable monetary benefits, deductions u/s 16(ia)/(ii)/(iii), and the employer's PF contribution · Motor car: where the statutory value (₹1,800 / ₹2,400 plus ₹600 / ₹900 for a driver) applies, the amount charged from the employee is NOT deducted · Interest-free loan: nothing taxable while the aggregate loan does not exceed ₹20,000, or for treatment of a Rule 3A disease; otherwise interest at the SBI rate prevailing on the FIRST day of the P.Y. for a loan of the same purpose, on the maximum outstanding monthly balance, less interest actually paid · Gifts: taxable for ALL employees, but gifts, vouchers or tokens up to ₹5,000 in aggregate during the P.Y. are exempt · Use of a movable asset: 10% of original cost if owned, actual hire charges if hired · Transfer of a movable asset: original cost − accumulated depreciation for each COMPLETED YEAR of employer use (running from the date of purchase, not from 1st April) − amount charged from the employee · ESOP [17(2)(vi)]: FMV on the date the OPTION IS EXERCISED − the amount actually paid by or recovered from the assessee · Timing split: an obligation of the employee met by the employer [17(2)(iv)] is taxed on CASH basis; a sum payable to effect an assurance or annuity [17(2)(v)] on ACCRUAL basis.
Provident FundFour components — employer's contribution, employee's contribution, interest on each — taxed differently across SPF / RPF / URPF / PPF. RPF: employer's contribution exempt up to 12% of salary, excess taxable; interest exempt @ 9.5% p.a. u/s 10(12), excess taxable as salary; lump-sum withdrawal exempt u/s 10(12) · SPF: employer's contribution and interest not taxable u/s 10(11); withdrawal exempt · URPF: employer's contribution and its interest taxed as Salaries on withdrawal; the employee's own contribution is not taxable (no deduction was ever allowed); interest on the employee's contribution is taxed under Income from Other Sources · PPF: minimum ₹500 a year, maximum ₹1,50,000 qualifying for 80C (old regime); interest exempt u/s 10(11) · Sec. 10(11)/(12) cap w.e.f. 01-04-2021: interest on the employee's own contribution above ₹2,50,000 a year is not exempt where the employer also contributes, and above ₹5,00,000 where the employer does not [Rule 9D, separate taxable/non-taxable accounts].
Deductions [Sec. 16]Only two deductions reach Taxable Salary. 16(ia) Standard deduction — LOWER of ₹50,000 (old regime) / ₹75,000 (default regime) or gross salary, allowed to ALL employees · 16(ii) Entertainment allowance — MINIMUM of actual allowance, ₹5,000, or 20% of basic salary; only for a GOVERNMENT employee, only under the old regime, and only after the allowance has first been fully included in taxable salary · 16(iii) Professional tax levied by a State under Article 276 — allowed on CASH basis, old regime only; where the employer pays it, it goes in once as a perquisite and out once as this deduction · Net Salary = Gross Salary − employee's PF contribution − TDS − loan repayment − other deductions from salary.

2.2 Income from House Property

Computation of Income from House Property — the fixed ladder [Sec. 22–24]
Particulars₹
Gross Annual Value (GAV) — see the four-step test below****
Less: Municipal tax — actually PAID, by the OWNER, in the P.Y. (unpaid tax, tenant-paid tax and advance tax are all inadmissible)(***)
Net Annual Value (NAV)****
Less: Sec. 24(a) Standard deduction — 30% of NAV, irrespective of actual expenditure; not available where NAV is nil or negative(***)
Less: Sec. 24(b) Interest on borrowed capital — on ACCRUAL basis, even if books are kept on cash basis(***)
Income from House Property****

GAV in four steps — Step 1: Reasonable Expected Rent (RER, also called Annual Letting Value) = LOWER of [HIGHER of Gross Municipal Value and Fair Rent] and [Standard Rent]. Step 2: Actual Rent Received/Receivable − current-year Unrealised Rent. Step 3: GAV = HIGHER of Step 1 and Step 2. Step 4: where Step 2 is lower ONLY because of VACANCY, Step 2 itself becomes the GAV.

Standard Rent CAPS the RER — it can never push RER up. In the metro cities (Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai) municipal tax is charged on Net Municipal Value: NMV = GMV − 10% of GMV − sewerage/water tax; in non-metro cities GMV = NMV. Outstanding rent is counted in Actual Rent; advance rent is not. Municipal tax paid by the tenant and notional interest on the tenant's deposit do not adjust de-facto rent. De facto rent = Actual Rent Receivable − cost of amenities.

Interest u/s 24(b) — Pre-construction period interest is accumulated and allowed in 5 equal instalments from the year construction is completed; the current year's interest is allowed in full in that year.

Pre-construction period starts on the day construction commenced or the day of borrowing, whichever is LATER, and ends on the 31st March immediately prior to the year of completion. Interest on a fresh loan taken to repay the original qualifying loan is allowed; interest on a loan taken to pay outstanding interest, brokerage for arranging the loan, and interest on a loan taken to pay municipal tax are all disallowed.

Self-occupied property [Sec. 23(2)] — NAV is Nil, Sec. 24(a) is unavailable, and the only deduction is interest u/s 24(b), capped at ₹2,00,000 (loan for acquisition/construction on or after 1-4-1999, completed within 5 years from the end of the F.Y. of borrowing, with the lender's certificate) or ₹30,000 in any other case.

A maximum of TWO houses may be treated as self-occupied, at the assessee's option, changeable every year; the rest are deemed to be let out. The ceiling is an AGGREGATE limit across both self-occupied houses, not per house, and the deduction is available only under the OLD regime. Available only to an Individual or HUF — never to a company or firm. Sec. 25A: recovery of arrears of rent or unrealised rent is taxable in the YEAR OF RECEIPT at 70% of the amount received (a flat 30% standard deduction), whether or not the assessee still owns the property.

2.3 Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

RuleThe formula, exactly
The schemeSec. 28 charges the income · Sec. 30–37 allow deductions · Sec. 40 / 40A / 43B disallow or defer specific items. The default direction is OPPOSITE for the two kinds of spend: capital expenditure is disallowed by default (deductible only where expressly allowed — Sec. 35 scientific research, Sec. 35AD), revenue expenditure is allowed by default (disallowed only where expressly barred). Sec. 30 and Sec. 31 cover only rent/rates/taxes/repairs/insurance of buildings and repairs/insurance of plant, machinery and furniture — RENT paid to use plant, machinery or furniture falls under the residuary Sec. 37(1).
Depreciation [Sec. 32]Computed on the Written Down Value of a BLOCK of assets [Sec. 2(11) — same nature AND same rate], never asset by asset: Opening WDV + assets of that block acquired during the P.Y. − money payable and scrap value of assets of that block sold/discarded/demolished/destroyed (capped at the additions figure) = WDV, which can never be negative; depreciation = prescribed % of that WDV. Sale proceeds exceeding (Opening WDV + additions) → the excess is short-term capital GAIN; a positive block balance with no asset left in it → short-term capital LOSS — in both cases no depreciation is charged · 180-day rule: depreciation is restricted to 50% of the normal rate only where the asset was BOTH acquired during the current P.Y. AND put to use for less than 180 days in that same P.Y.; the date of SALE has no significance at all · Additional depreciation [Sec. 32(1)(iia)] = 20% of actual cost, split 10% this year and 10% the next where the asset was acquired and put to use for less than 180 days · Sec. 43A adjusts the ACTUAL COST of a specific imported asset for exchange-rate movement on payment; Sec. 43AA taxes or allows forex gain/loss generally, per ICDS, and steps aside wherever 43A applies.
DisallowancesSec. 40A(3): payment exceeding ₹10,000 in a day otherwise than by account payee cheque/DD, ECS or prescribed electronic mode → 100% disallowed; the limit rises to ₹35,000 for a road transport operator plying, hiring or leasing goods carriages · Sec. 43B allows Category A items (tax, duty, cess, bonus, specified interest, leave encashment, PF etc.) if paid by the Sec. 139(1) due date; Category B (dues to micro/small enterprises beyond the Sec. 15 MSMED Act time limit) gets NO such relief — deduction follows the P.Y. of actual payment · Employer's own PF/gratuity/superannuation contribution [36(1)(iv)/(v)] follows the 43B return-filing due date; employees' contributions withheld from wages [36(1)(va)] are deductible only if credited by the due date fixed under the relevant labour law · CSR spend is disallowed under Sec. 37(1) alone — if the same spend independently qualifies under Sec. 30 to 36, it stays deductible there · Special reserve [Sec. 36(1)(viii)] = LEAST of (a) amount transferred during the P.Y., (b) 20% of profits of the specified long-term-finance business, (c) twice the paid-up share capital plus general reserve.
Books, audit & presumptiveSec. 44AB has no single ₹1 crore line — the threshold rises to ₹2 crore, ₹3 crore or ₹10 crore depending on whether income is declared u/s 44AD and how much turnover moves through cash · Sec. 44AD (resident individual/HUF/firm, not LLP, not a profession, not commission/brokerage/agency, not a Sec. 44AE business): turnover up to ₹2 crore, or up to ₹3 crore where cash receipts are 5% or less of total turnover. Estimated income = 6% of receipts through account payee cheque/DD, ECS or prescribed electronic modes; 8% of everything else. Sec. 44AD(4) locks the assessee out of the scheme for 5 A.Y.s if he declares a lower profit within 5 A.Y.s of opting in · Sec. 44ADA (resident individual/firm, not LLP, Sec. 44AA profession): gross receipts up to ₹50 lakh, or up to ₹75 lakh where cash receipts are 5% or less — estimated income = a FLAT 50% of gross receipts, whatever the mode of collection · Sec. 44AE (not more than 10 goods carriages at any time in the P.Y.): ₹1,000 per ton of gross vehicle weight per month or part month for a heavy goods vehicle (GVW above 12,000 kg); ₹7,500 per month or part month for any other, counted from the month of acquisition whether put to use or not · In all three, no further deduction u/s 30 to 38, and depreciation is deemed already allowed.
Deemed income & firm assessmentSec. 115BBE: income referred to in Sec. 68 to 69D is taxed at a flat 60% + surcharge 25% + cess, with NO deduction for any expenditure or allowance and NO set-off of any loss · Sec. 40(b) remuneration to partners — in case of LOSS, maximum ₹3,00,000; in case of PROFIT, on the first ₹6,00,000 of book profit, 90% of book profit or ₹3,00,000 whichever is HIGHER, and 60% on the balance book profit · Interest to a sole PROPRIETOR is fully disallowed; interest to a PARTNER is allowed only within the Sec. 40(b) cap; interest to a RELATIVE is allowed subject to Sec. 40A(2).

2.4 Capital Gains

Capital Gain [Sec. 48] = Full value of consideration − Expenses on transfer − Cost of acquisition − Cost of improvement − Exemption u/s 54, 54B, 54D, etc.

Securities Transaction Tax paid is NEVER deductible in computing income under "Capital gains." Sec. 45 charges the gain in the year of transfer; Sec. 2(14) defines the capital asset; Sec. 2(47) defines transfer.

Indexed cost of acquisition = Cost of acquisition × (CII of the year of transfer ÷ CII of the year of acquisition, or of F.Y. 2001-02, whichever is LATER). Indexed cost of improvement = Cost of improvement × (CII of the year of transfer ÷ CII of the year of improvement).

The Cost Inflation Index is notified having regard to 75% of the average rise in the Consumer Price Index (urban) for the preceding previous year.

Period of holding — Short-Term Capital Asset [Sec. 2(42A)] = held for NOT MORE THAN 24 months; but NOT MORE THAN 12 months for a security listed in India, a unit of an equity-oriented fund, a Zero-Coupon Bond, a UTI unit, or a unit of a listed debt-oriented mutual fund. A Long-Term Capital Asset [Sec. 2(29A)] is simply an asset that is not short-term.

Two assets stay short-term whatever the holding period: a depreciable asset in a Sec. 32 block [Sec. 50] and a market-linked debenture or unit of a specified mutual fund [Sec. 50AA]. The date of transfer is excluded when counting the period of holding.

ChargeRate and rule
STCG u/s 111AEquity share, unit of an equity-oriented fund or unit of a business trust, transaction chargeable to STT — taxed at 20% + surcharge + cess. No Chapter VI-A deduction against it. For a resident individual/HUF whose other income falls below the exemption limit: Tax = 20% × [such STCG − (Exempted ceiling − Total income excluding such STCG)].
LTCG u/s 112AUp to ₹1,25,000 → Nil; the excess at 12.5% plus surcharge and cess. Rebate u/s 87A is NOT available against this tax in either regime. For a resident individual/HUF the gain is first reduced by any shortfall in the basic exemption limit.
Land / building, the optionFor a resident individual/HUF transferring land, building or both, acquired BEFORE 23-07-2024 and transferred ON OR AFTER that date: Option 1 — tax @ 12.5% WITHOUT indexation, or Option 2 — tax @ 20% AFTER indexation. The option governs only the TAX; the capital gain itself is always first computed without index benefit. No other class of LTCG carries this option.
Sec. 54-series exemptions54 — LT residential house → one residential house in India (two, if the gain does not exceed ₹2 crore, once in a lifetime); 1 year before / 2 years after for purchase, 3 years after for construction; CGAS available · 54B — agricultural land (ST or LT) used at least 2 years → new agricultural land within 2 years; CGAS · 54D — compulsorily acquired industrial land/building used at least 2 years → new land/building within 3 years of receiving compensation; CGAS · 54EC — LT land or building → 5-year NHAI/REC/PFC/IRFC/IREDA bonds within 6 months, hard ceiling ₹50 lakh, NO CGAS option · 54F — any LT asset other than a residential house → one residential house in India (assessee owning not more than one other house); same time limits as Sec. 54; the deduction is PROPORTIONATE to net sale consideration, not simply the lower of the two · 54G / 54GA — shifting an urban industrial undertaking to a non-urban area / an SEZ; 1 year before to 3 years after; CGAS · Everywhere except 54F the deduction is the LOWER of qualifying investment and capital gain. Unutilised money must be deposited in the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme, 1988 by the return due date, or it becomes chargeable in the year the time limit expires.
Special computationsSec. 45(1A) insurance claim · Sec. 45(4) r.w.s. 9B on dissolution/reconstitution: A = B + C − D, where B is money received by the specified person, C the FMV of the capital asset received, and D the balance in his capital account excluding any increase from revaluation or self-generated goodwill (if A is negative it is deemed Nil) · Sec. 45(5) compulsory acquisition · Sec. 45(5A) joint development agreements · Sec. 46 liquidation and Sec. 46A buy-back · Sec. 50C (land/building stamp duty value) and Sec. 50CA (unquoted shares) · Sec. 51 advance money forfeited · Sec. 55(2)(a) self-generated assets · Sec. 55(2)(aa)(iiia) bonus shares · Sec. 94(8) bonus stripping — the ignored loss becomes the deemed cost of the bonus units still held.

2.5 Income from Other Sources

ItemRate and rule
The head itselfSec. 56(1) is RESIDUARY — a receipt lands here only if it is taxable income AND does not fall under any of the other four heads.
Casual incomeWinnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, gambling, betting and online gaming are taxed FLAT at 30% + surcharge + Health & Education Cess @ 4% under Sec. 115BB (online games separately, Sec. 115BBJ), with Sec. 58(4) blocking every deduction — no expenditure, no Sec. 80C to 80U, and no unexhausted basic exemption limit. TDS on lottery/horse-race winnings is skipped only where the amount does not exceed ₹10,000; where only the net receipt is given, gross it up — net received = 70% of gross winnings.
Gifts [Sec. 56(2)(x)]Immovable property gifts are tested PER INCIDENCE against a ₹50,000 stamp duty value; cash and movable-property gifts are AGGREGATED across the whole previous year against the same ₹50,000 · A concessional purchase of immovable property is taxable to the buyer only where the stamp duty value exceeds the consideration by more than the HIGHER of ₹50,000 or 10% of consideration · Exempt regardless of amount: gifts from a defined "relative" (spouse; siblings of self or spouse; siblings of either parent; lineal ascendants and descendants of self or spouse; and their spouses — a closed list), gifts on the individual's own marriage, under a will or inheritance, in contemplation of death, or from a local authority.
Other charges & deductionsFamily pension — taxable here after a standard deduction u/s 57(iia) of the LOWER of one-third of the pension or the statutory rupee ceiling; a pension received by the employee himself stays taxable as Salaries · Interest on compensation or enhanced compensation [Sec. 56(2)(viii) with Sec. 57(iv)] — taxed in the year of RECEIPT, never accrual, after a flat 50% deduction · Dividend [Sec. 2(22)] — the only deduction is interest expense, capped at 20% of the dividend income for the year; no deduction at all against dividend taxed under the buy-back clause, Sec. 2(22)(f) · Sec. 56(2)(ii)/(iii) letting of machinery, plant or furniture and composite rent, with Sec. 57(ii)/(iii) deductions · Sec. 59 deemed profits mirror Sec. 41(1).

Module 3: Total Income & Tax Liability of Individuals & HUF (15%)

TopicThe Ladder
3.1 Clubbing [Sec. 60–65]Sec. 60 — transfer of income without transferring the asset · Sec. 61–63 — revocable transfers · Sec. 64(1)(ii) — remuneration to a spouse from a concern in which the individual has a substantial interest · Sec. 64(1)(iv)/(vii) — income from an asset transferred to a spouse, or to an AOP/other person, without adequate consideration · Sec. 64(1A) — a minor child's income is clubbed with the PARENT whose total income is higher, regardless of who transferred the underlying asset to the minor; Sec. 10(32) then exempts the MINIMUM of ₹1,500 or the income clubbed, separately for each child, under the old regime only · Sec. 64(2) — conversion of self-acquired property into HUF property · Sec. 65 — the transferee is jointly liable for the tax on clubbed income · Where a transferred asset is invested in a business: income clubbed = income of the business × (value of the transferred asset on the 1st day of the P.Y. ÷ total investment by the transferee on the same day); for a firm the same fraction is applied to interest on capital.
3.2 Set-off, orderIntra-head / inter-source [Sec. 70] → Inter-head [Sec. 71] → Carry forward. Sec. 70 exceptions: long-term capital loss only against long-term capital gain (short-term capital loss goes against either); speculation loss only against speculation profit; Sec. 35AD specified-business loss only against another specified business; race-horse loss only against that activity; a loss from a Sec. 10-exempt source is never set off; nothing at all can be set off against casual income or Sec. 68/69A–69D income. Every restriction runs ONE WAY — income from these sources still absorbs losses from other sources of the same head · Sec. 71 exceptions: a CAPITAL GAINS loss can never go against another head (though other heads' losses can go against capital gains); speculation and Sec. 35AD losses are likewise one-directional · The Act prescribes no priority for inter-head set-off — adjust losses that cannot be carried forward FIRST, since any unabsorbed balance is lost forever.
3.2 Carry forwardHouse property [Sec. 71B] — 8 A.Y.s, only against house-property income; allowed even from a BELATED return; under the default regime it cannot be set off inter-head nor carried forward at all · Business, non-speculative [Sec. 72] — 8 A.Y.s, only against PGBP; the business need not continue · Speculation [Sec. 73] — 4 A.Y.s, only against speculation profit · Sec. 35AD specified business [Sec. 73A] — no time limit, against any specified business · Capital loss [Sec. 74] — 8 A.Y.s; long-term only against long-term, short-term against either · Race horses [Sec. 74A] — 4 A.Y.s, only against the same activity, which must still be carried on · Unabsorbed depreciation [Sec. 32(2)] — no time limit, against ANY income except Salaries and casual income, and it survives a late return · Every other head's carry forward requires a return filed within the Sec. 139(1)/139(3) due date [Sec. 80] · Sec. 78 reduces only the retiring partner's LOSS share on a change in constitution — unabsorbed depreciation is carved out and survives in full.
3.3 Chapter VI-A ceilings80C minimum of eligible contributions or ₹1,50,000 · 80CCC pension fund, ₹1,50,000 · 80CCD(1) lower of amount paid or 10% of salary (salaried) / 20% of GTI (others); 80CCD(1B) an additional ₹50,000; 80CCD(2) employer's contribution up to 10% of salary (14% for Central/State Government) · 80CCE caps 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) at ₹1,50,000 — 80CCD(1B) and 80CCD(2) sit OUTSIDE and ABOVE that ceiling · 80CCH Agnipath/Agniveer Corpus Fund · 80D medical insurance, the enhanced ₹50,000 limit turning on the age of the INSURED, not the payer · 80DD ₹75,000 (40% to under 80% disability) / ₹1,25,000 (80% or more) for a dependant disabled relative · 80DDB minimum of actual expenditure or ₹40,000, raised to ₹1,00,000 where the patient is a senior citizen, reduced by insurance/employer reimbursement · 80E whole interest on an education loan, no ceiling, for 8 consecutive years from the year repayment begins · 80EE ₹50,000 · 80EEA ₹1,50,000 · 80EEB electric vehicle loan interest, ₹1,50,000 · 80G = (100%/50% of Category A donations) + (100%/50% of Category B donations, capped at 10% of Adjusted GTI), where Adjusted GTI = GTI − LTCG − STCG u/s 111A − all 80C–80U deductions other than 80G − Sec. 115A/115AB/115AC incomes (casual income stays IN) · 80GG minimum of ₹5,000 p.m., 25% of Adjusted GTI, or rent paid − 10% of Adjusted GTI · 80GGA 100% · 80GGB/80GGC political contributions · 80JJAA 30% of additional employee cost for 3 A.Y.s · 80LA 100% for 10 consecutive years · 80M minimum of dividend received or dividend distributed by the due date · 80QQB / 80RRB minimum of the income or ₹3,00,000 · 80TTA / 80TTB interest on deposits · 80U ₹75,000 / ₹1,25,000 for the assessee's own disability — claimable alongside 80DD for a different person · Chapter VI-A deductions attach only to the "remaining GTI" — never to LTCG, STCG u/s 111A or casual income · Relief u/s 89 [Rule 21A] is a reduction in TAX, computed after cess — never a deduction from Total Income.
3.4 Regimes, AMT & HUFDefault regime [Sec. 115BAC(1A)] blocks Sec. 10(5) LTC, 10(13A) HRA, 10(14) special allowances, 10(17), 10(32), 10AA, Sec. 16 entertainment allowance and professional tax (standard deduction of ₹75,000 survives), 24(b) interest on a SELF-OCCUPIED property (let-out property interest survives), 32(1)(iia), 32AD, 33AB/33ABA, 35(1)(ii)/(iia)/(iii) and 35(2AA), 35AD, 35CCC, and all of Chapter VI-A except 80CCD(2), 80CCH(2), 80JJAA and 80LA · A person WITHOUT business/profession income may move between regimes year to year; a person WITH business income who opts for the old regime u/s 115BAC(6) is locked in, may withdraw only ONCE, and can never opt out again while the business income continues · AMT [Sec. 115JC] = 18.5% of Adjusted Total Income, where Adjusted Total Income = Total Income + deductions u/s 80H to 80RRB (other than 80P) + Sec. 35AD deduction less Sec. 32 depreciation + Sec. 10AA deduction; liability = HIGHER of regular tax and AMT, plus cess. AMT does not apply where tax is computed u/s 115BAC(1A), nor where Adjusted Total Income does not exceed ₹20 lakh; credit is available u/s 115JD · HUF: Sec. 171 partition — a partial partition occurring after 31-12-1978 is barred from being recorded by Sec. 171(9); the family continues to be assessed as one HUF, every member remaining jointly and severally liable.
3.5 Advance taxSec. 208 — payable in the previous year itself once the estimated liability is ₹10,000 or more. Sec. 211 instalments: an eligible assessee in an eligible business u/s 44AD or 44ADA pays 100% by 15th March in a single instalment; every other assessee pays up to 15% by 15th June, up to 45% by 15th September, up to 75% by 15th December, up to 100% by 15th March · Sec. 209 ladder: estimated GTI − Chapter VIA per the regime opted = estimated Total Income → gross tax − rebate u/s 87A → add surcharge and cess → less TDS/TCS. A resident senior citizen with no PGBP income is not liable to advance tax at all; net agricultural income still enters the estimate; failure to pay an instalment makes the assessee an assessee in default [Sec. 218]; shortfall or deferment draws interest u/s 234B / 234C.
3.6 TDS thresholds [Chapter XVII-B]192 salary, average rate · 192A EPF 10%, ₹50,000 · 193 interest on securities 10%, ₹10,000 · 194 dividend 10%, ₹10,000 · 194A other interest 10% — ₹10,000 generally, ₹50,000 for a bank/co-operative bank/post office, ₹1,00,000 where the payee is a senior citizen · 194B lottery/crossword/card games 30%, ₹10,000 per single transaction · 194BA online games, same rate, NIL threshold · 194BB horse races, ₹10,000 per single transaction · 194C 1% (individual/HUF payee) / 2% (others) — skipped only if the single contract is ₹30,000 or less AND the year's aggregate is ₹1,00,000 or less · 194D insurance commission 10%/2%, ₹20,000 · 194DA 2%, ₹1,00,000 · 194EE 10%, ₹2,500 · 194G 2%, ₹20,000 · 194H 2%, ₹20,000 · 194-I rent — 2% for plant/machinery/equipment, 10% for land/building/furniture/fittings, ₹50,000 per month or part · 194-IA 1% of consideration or stamp duty value, whichever higher, skipped only if BOTH are below ₹50 lakh · 194-IB 2%, ₹50,000 per month · 194-IC 10% · 194J 10% (2% for call-centre FTS and certain film royalty), ₹50,000 tested on the AGGREGATE, not per bill · 194K 10%, ₹10,000 · 194LA 10%, ₹5,00,000 · 194M 2%, ₹50 lakh · 194N cash withdrawal, ₹1 crore (₹3 crore for a co-operative society; ₹20 lakh for a defaulter) · 194-O 0.1% · 194P specified senior citizen aged 75+ · 194Q 0.1% of the sum exceeding ₹50 lakh, where the buyer's preceding-year turnover exceeds ₹10 crore · 194R 10%, ₹20,000 · 194S 1% · 194T firm's payment to a partner 10%, ₹20,000 · Sec. 206AA — no PAN, deduct at the HIGHEST of the section rate, the rate in force, or 20% (5% under 194-O/194-Q) · Sec. 206CC — no PAN for TCS, collect at the HIGHER of twice the specified rate or 5% · Sec. 201(1) deems a non-deductor or non-depositor an "assessee in default."
3.7–3.9 Returns, PAN, assessmentDue dates [Explanation 2 to Sec. 139(1)]: 30th November for Sec. 92E transfer-pricing cases · 31st October for audit-required assessees and companies without international transactions · 31st July for any other case · Sec. 234F fee ₹1,000 where income is up to ₹5 lakh, ₹5,000 above · Belated [139(4)] and revised [139(5)] returns share one outer window — 31st December of the A.Y. or completion of assessment, whichever is earlier · Updated return [139(8A)] — 48 months from the end of the A.Y., but never a loss return, never reducing tax or creating a refund, with additional income-tax of 25% / 50% / 60% / 70% u/s 140B by delay slab · Defective return [139(9)] — 15 days to rectify, extendable · Companies and firms file irrespective of income; "any other person" files where pre-Chapter-VIA, pre-Sec.-54-series income exceeds the basic exemption limit, plus compulsory filing for foreign assets or 7th-proviso/Rule 12AB triggers (turnover above ₹60 lakh, TDS+TCS of ₹25,000 or more) · PAN — a 10-character alphanumeric code, one per person [Sec. 139A]; compulsory where income exceeds the exemption limit or turnover is likely to exceed ₹5,00,000; default draws a ₹10,000 penalty u/s 272B; an unlinked PAN is inoperative from 1.7.2023 · Self-assessment tax [Sec. 140A] must be paid BEFORE filing; a shortfall is applied first to fee, then interest, then tax · Intimation u/s 143(1) must issue within 9 months from the end of the financial year of filing; where nothing is payable or refundable, the acknowledgment itself is deemed the intimation · Beyond that: Scrutiny [143(3)], Best Judgment [144], Income Escaping Assessment [147].
Section B · Indirect Taxation (50%)

Module 4: Concept of Indirect Taxes (5%)

TopicThe Ladder
4.1–4.2 Nature & contrastAn indirect tax's burden SHIFTS from the seller (who pays it to Government) to the buyer/consumer (who ultimately bears it) — the "no pinch" feature · Indirect taxes are REGRESSIVE (the same percentage burden on rich and poor alike); direct taxes are PROGRESSIVE · Incidence and impact: a direct tax falls on the SAME person — it cannot be shifted and it pinches; an indirect tax falls on DIFFERENT persons — it can be shifted and does not pinch · The source's own examples: Income Tax = direct; GST and Customs Duty = indirect. Taxable event: direct = the assessee's taxable income; indirect = supply of goods and services.
4.3 Pre-GST structureArticle 246 read with Schedule VII divides legislative subject matter into three lists — Union (List I), State (List II), Concurrent (List III) · Entry 84 (Union) = Central Excise on tobacco and other manufactured goods, alcohol and most narcotics excluded · Entry 92A (Union) = Central Sales Tax on inter-State sale/purchase · Entry 54 (State) = State-level VAT · Entry 51 (State) = State excise on alcohol, opium and narcotics manufactured in the State · Pre-GST indirect tax was fragmented across excise duty, service tax, VAT, CST, purchase tax, entertainment tax and octroi, with tax nakas at every inter-State border · Cascading ("tax on tax") arose because ITC of Excise Duty and CST was NOT available to the next dealer — the source's own illustration puts pre-GST total tax at ₹29,149 against ₹13,200 under GST on the identical ₹1,00,000 + ₹10,000 chain.
4.4 Constitutional validityConstitution (122nd Amendment) Bill introduced 19.12.2014 → Lok Sabha May 2015 → Rajya Sabha Select Committee report 22.07.2015 → both Houses August 2016 → President's assent 8th September 2016 → enacted as the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, effective 16th September 2016 · GST is a DUAL GST: CGST + SGST/UTGST concurrently, plus IGST under Parliament's exclusive power on inter-State supply and imports · GST Council decisions need at least 3/4 of the weighted votes of members present and voting; the Centre carries 1/3 weightage and all States together 2/3 — so the Centre plus a minimum of 20 States are needed for a majority. Quorum = one-half of the total members.

Module 5: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Laws (35%) — the largest module in this paper

TopicThe Ladder
5.1 FrameworkGST is a destination-based, multi-stage, dual-structure value-added tax administered through one common portal; tax paid at the previous stage is credited at the next, so only the value addition is finally taxed · Article 279A constitutes the GST Council; Article 269A governs levy and collection on inter-State supply · IGST rate = CGST rate + SGST rate — an 18% IGST on an inter-State supply becomes CGST 9% + SGST/UTGST 9% intra-State · Compensation payable to a State = Projected Revenue for the F.Y. − Actual Revenue earned (including its IGST share), with F.Y. 2015-16 as the base year and an assumed growth rate of 14% p.a.; at the end of the transition period 50% of the unutilised Fund goes to the Consolidated Fund of India and 50% to the States · Compensation Cess is levied on notified goods (pan masala, tobacco, coal, aerated water, motor cars) and is extended up to 31/03/2026 · Staying OUTSIDE GST: Basic Customs Duty, Export Duty, Anti-Dumping and Safeguard Duty, R&D Cess (Central); State Excise Duty, Stamp Duty, Profession Tax and Motor Vehicle Tax (State); plus alcoholic liquor for human consumption.
5.2 Supply & chargeA transaction is a supply [Sec. 7] only if ALL hold: supply of goods or services or both · for consideration (subject to exceptions) · in the course or furtherance of business (subject to exceptions) · a TAXABLE supply · in a taxable territory · by a taxable person · Schedule I — deemed supply even WITHOUT consideration: disposal of an ITC-availed asset, supply between related or distinct persons (separately-registered branches are distinct persons), principal-agent goods transfer, and import of services from a related person or one's own foreign establishment · Schedule II classifies activities as goods OR services (renting is always a service; transfer of title in goods is always goods) · Schedule III is the negative list — neither goods nor services: employee services to the employer, court/tribunal services, sale of land, sale of a completed building; but actionable claims in lottery, betting, gambling, horse racing and online money gaming are carved BACK IN as taxable supply of goods · Sec. 8: a COMPOSITE supply (naturally bundled, one predominant element) is taxed at the PRINCIPAL supply's rate; a MIXED supply is taxed at the HIGHEST rate among its constituents — a single price alone decides nothing · Sec. 9(1) forward charge is the default; 9(3) reverse charge, 9(4) supplies from unregistered persons, and 9(5) e-commerce operators are NOTIFIED exceptions only · CGST is levied on all intra-State supplies except alcoholic liquor for human consumption, un-denatured extra neutral alcohol and rectified spirit used to make it, on the Sec. 15 value, at rates not exceeding 20%.
The four "no tax" categoriesZero-rated supply [Sec. 16, IGST Act] — export of goods or services, or supply to an SEZ developer/unit for authorised operations: ITC may be availed and unutilised ITC refunded even though the outward supply bears no tax · Exempt supply [Sec. 2(47)] — supply attracting a NIL rate of tax, or wholly exempted u/s 11 CGST / Sec. 6 IGST, and it INCLUDES non-taxable supply; no ITC · Nil-rated supply — taxable in principle but at a nil rate; excluded, with exempt supply, from a composition trader's taxable turnover · Non-taxable supply [Sec. 2(78)] — not leviable to tax at all under the CGST or IGST Act, e.g. alcoholic liquor for human consumption. Only zero-rating preserves the credit chain.
5.2.5 Composition levy [Sec. 10]A registered person whose aggregate turnover in the PRECEDING F.Y. did not exceed the threshold may pay, in lieu of tax u/s 9(1): 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) for manufacturers other than of ice cream, pan masala, tobacco and aerated water · 1% for traders, on taxable turnover of goods and services in the State/UT · 5% (2.5% + 2.5%) for restaurant services · 6% (3% + 3%) for other services · For manufacturers "turnover" includes exempted supplies; for traders it does not · All registrations under the SAME PAN must opt in together — one ineligible unit disqualifies every unit · No inter-State outward supply (an export is an inter-State supply and destroys eligibility), no supply of non-leviable goods, no services through a TCS-collecting e-commerce operator, not a casual or non-resident taxable person · Reverse-charge liability is discharged at the NORMAL rate, in cash, with no ITC — never at the composition rate — and the value of those inward supplies stays out of aggregate turnover.
5.3.1 Time of supplyGoods, forward charge [Sec. 12(2)] = EARLIER of the date of issue of invoice or the last date on which the invoice was required to be issued u/s 31 — Notification No. 66/2017-CT dated 15/11/2017 relieves a non-composition registered person from paying GST on an ADVANCE for goods · Goods, reverse charge [Sec. 12(3)] = EARLIEST of the date of receipt of goods, the date of payment entered in the recipient's books, the date payment is debited to his bank, or the day immediately following 30 days from the supplier's invoice — the advance relief does NOT apply here · Services, forward charge [Sec. 13(2)] — invoice issued within the Sec. 31 period: earlier of invoice date or receipt of payment; invoice NOT issued in time: earlier of the date of provision of service or receipt of payment; otherwise the date the recipient shows receipt in his books · Services, reverse charge [Sec. 13(3)] = EARLIER of the date of payment in the recipient's books, the date of bank debit, or the day immediately following 60 days from the supplier's invoice · Residual [12(5)/13(5)]: the due date of the periodical return, else the date the tax is paid · Enhancement in value by interest, late fee or penalty [12(6)/13(6)]: the date the supplier RECEIVES that addition.
5.3.2 Place of supplyPlace of supply decides WHETHER a transaction is intra-State (CGST + SGST/UTGST) or inter-State (IGST) — it does not by itself decide the rate or the taxability · Sec. 10 IGST — goods not imported or exported; Sec. 11 — goods imported into or exported from India; Sec. 12 — services where supplier and recipient are both in India; Sec. 13 — services where either is outside India · Sec. 10(1)(b) bill-to-ship-to: where goods are delivered on the direction of a THIRD person, that third person is DEEMED to have received them and the place of supply is his PRINCIPAL PLACE OF BUSINESS, not the physical delivery address · Sec. 9, IGST Act: where the supplier's location or the place of supply is in territorial waters, it is deemed to be in the coastal State/UT nearest the appropriate baseline · Sec. 7 IGST defines inter-State supply; Sec. 8 defines intra-State supply.
5.3.3 Value of supplyValue of taxable supply [Sec. 15] = Transaction value + Sec. 15(2) inclusions − Sec. 15(3) discounts, provided price is the sole consideration and the parties are not related · ADD: taxes, duties, cesses and fees under any law OTHER than GST if charged separately (TCS under the Income-tax Act is NOT added — it is an interim levy); amounts the supplier was liable to pay but the recipient paid; incidental expenses charged before delivery; interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment; and subsidies directly linked to the price, EXCEPT Central and State Government subsidies · A post-supply discount is deductible only if all three Sec. 15(3)(b) conditions are met together · Valuation rules: Rule 27 consideration not wholly in money (open market value → money plus money-equivalent → like kind and quality → Rule 30/31) · Rule 28 distinct/related persons (invoice value is deemed OMV where the recipient is eligible for full ITC; 90% of the recipient's onward price where goods are for further supply as such) · Rule 29 supply through an agent · Rule 30 = 110% of cost of production, acquisition or provision · Rule 31 residual, reasonable means — for SERVICES the supplier may go straight to Rule 31, skipping Rule 30 · Rule 31A lottery = higher of 100/140 of face value or 100/140 of the price notified by the organising State; betting/gambling/horse racing = 100% of the face value of the bet · Rule 32(2) foreign currency · Rule 32(4) life insurance (gross premium less the investment allocation; 10% of a single-premium annuity; otherwise 25% of first-year and 12.5% of later premiums) · Rule 32(5) margin scheme for second-hand goods with no ITC availed = Selling Price − Purchase Price, a negative margin ignored · Rule 32(6) vouchers are valued at the MONEY VALUE of what is redeemable, not the purchase price · Rule 33 pure agent costs are excluded only if all three conditions hold.
TopicThe Ladder
5.4 Input Tax CreditSec. 16(2) — all conditions apply TOGETHER, never in the alternative: (a) possession of a tax invoice or debit note from a registered supplier; (aa) the supplier has furnished those details in GSTR-1 and they have been communicated to the recipient u/s 37; (b) the goods or services have been RECEIVED; (c) the tax charged has actually been PAID to Government; (d) the recipient has furnished his own return · Sec. 16(4) bars ITC after the EARLIER of 30th November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice relates, or the date of furnishing the annual return (GSTR-9) · Sec. 16(3) — no ITC on the tax component where depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act · Rule 37 — fail to pay the supplier value plus tax within 180 days and the ITC is added back to output liability the following month, with interest up to 18% · Sec. 17(1) restricts credit to the business-use portion; Sec. 17(2) to the taxable-supply portion (zero-rated supplies count as taxable) · Sec. 17(5) BLOCKED CREDIT, a standalone override even where Sec. 16(1) is satisfied: (a) motor vehicles for transporting persons with approved seating capacity of 13 or fewer including the driver — except for further supply, passenger transport or driving training (vehicles seating more than 13 are freely creditable); (aa) vessels and aircraft, with parallel exceptions; (ab) their general insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance; (b) food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic and plastic surgery, leasing/renting/hiring of motor vehicles, vessels or aircraft, life and health insurance; (ii) club and health-and-fitness-centre membership; (iii) employee vacation travel benefits — the (b)/(ii)/(iii) block lifts where the employer is statutorily obliged to provide the benefit; (c) works contract services for construction of immovable property other than plant and machinery; (d) goods or services for construction of immovable property on OWN ACCOUNT, even if for business; (e) tax paid u/s 10 composition levy; (f) supplies to a non-resident taxable person, except goods imported by him; (fa) CSR obligations under Sec. 135 of the Companies Act, 2013; (g) personal consumption; (h) goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by gift or free sample; (i) tax paid u/s 74 for periods up to F.Y. 2023-24 · "Plant and machinery" in the (c)/(d) carve-out EXCLUDES land, buildings, other civil structures, telecommunication towers and pipelines laid outside the factory premises · Sec. 18 covers credit in special circumstances, Sec. 18(6) the pay-back on supplying capital goods (higher of ITC taken less prescribed percentage points, or tax on transaction value); Sec. 19 job work; Sec. 20/21 Input Service Distributor.
5.5 Computation & utilisationCompute output tax head-wise (intra-State → CGST + SGST/UTGST; inter-State → IGST), compute eligible ITC head-wise, then set off in the order prescribed by Sec. 49(5) read with Rule 88A and Sec. 49A; the shortfall is paid in cash through the Electronic Cash Ledger · IGST credit — first fully against IGST liability, then the balance against CGST and SGST/UTGST in any order and any proportion · CGST credit — first against CGST, then against IGST, but only after IGST credit is fully exhausted and before SGST credit is used against IGST; NEVER against SGST/UTGST · SGST/UTGST credit — first against SGST/UTGST, then against IGST, only after IGST credit is exhausted and only where no CGST balance is available; NEVER against CGST · Sec. 49A is a mandatory pre-condition: no CGST or SGST/UTGST credit may be used for ANY output liability until IGST credit is fully exhausted. Net GST payable in cash = gross output tax liability for the period − eligible ITC available for set-off, computed per head.
5.6 RegistrationPAN-based and State/UT-wise — operating from several States requires a separate GSTIN, and hence a separate set of electronic ledgers, for each · GSTIN is 15 digits: 1–2 State code, 3–12 PAN, 13–14 entity code for that PAN-holder within the State, 15 checksum · Sec. 22 thresholds — ₹40,00,000 for an exclusive supplier of goods outside the specified-goods list and outside the ten named States; ₹20,00,000 for a supplier of services, or of both goods and services, and for suppliers of ice cream and other edible ice, pan masala, tobacco and manufactured tobacco substitutes, fly ash bricks/blocks, bricks of fossil meals, building bricks and earthen or roofing tiles, and for intra-State suppliers in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Tripura and Uttarakhand; ₹10,00,000 in the special category States — which for GST registration means only Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura, not the Constitution's full 11-State list under Article 279A(4)(g) · Sec. 23 lists persons not liable; Sec. 24 requires compulsory registration irrespective of turnover; Sec. 25(3) allows voluntary registration · Procedure: Part A of FORM GST REG-01 → PAN validation and OTP → Temporary Reference Number → Part B with documents → acknowledgement in FORM GST REG-02 · Sec. 26 deemed registration · Sec. 27 casual and non-resident taxable persons · Sec. 28 amendment · Sec. 29 cancellation/suspension · Sec. 30 with Rule 23 revocation.
5.7 Invoice & e-way billGoods [Sec. 31(1)] — the invoice is tied to a physical EVENT: before or at removal where the goods move, before or at delivery where they do not · Services [Sec. 31(2) r.w. Rule 47] — tied to a TIME WINDOW: 30 days from the supply, stretched to 45 days only for insurance and banking companies, financial institutions and NBFCs. There is no 45-day rule for goods and no "removal" concept for services · e-Invoicing is mandatory once turnover exceeds ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18, tested PAN-wide across all GSTINs · HSN digits keyed to the PRECEDING year's turnover: up to ₹5 crore → 4-digit HSN, mandatory for B2B only; exceeding ₹5 crore → 6-digit HSN, for ALL transactions · ₹200 — the value below which no tax invoice or bill of supply is compulsory for an unregistered, non-requesting recipient (a consolidated invoice at the day's close instead) · ₹50,000 — the value at or above which an unregistered recipient's name and address must appear on the invoice [Rule 46(e)], and also the E-Way Bill trigger: Form GST EWB-01 is required where consignment value EXCEEDS ₹50,000, tested per invoice or on the aggregate carried in one conveyance · Two movements need an e-way bill even BELOW ₹50,000: inter-State movement to or from a job worker, and inter-State transport of handicraft goods by a registration-exempt dealer · Validity: other than over-dimensional cargo — 1 day for less than 200 km, plus 1 day for every additional 200 km or part; over-dimensional cargo — 1 day for less than 20 km, plus 1 day for every additional 20 km or part · An e-way bill can never be DELETED but may be CANCELLED by its generator within 24 hours, unless already verified by a proper officer · Sec. 34 governs credit and debit notes; Rule 46 the contents; Rules 48 and 54 the manner of issue and special cases; Sec. 68 with Rules 138 to 138E the e-way bill machinery.
5.8 Returns & paymentGSTR-1 — 11th of the next month for monthly filers, or by the 13th of the month following the quarter for QRMP filers · GSTR-3B — 20th of the next month for monthly filers, or by the 22nd (Category 1 States) / 24th (Category 2 States) of the month following the quarter for QRMP filers · GSTR-1/IFF is BLOCKED where a previous GSTR-1 is unfiled, the PRECEDING month's GSTR-3B is unfiled, a Rule 88C liability-mismatch or Rule 88D excess-ITC intimation is unresolved, or bank details under Rule 10A are not furnished [Sec. 37(4), Rule 59(6)] · Rectification of any error or omission in GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B is barred after 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier · GSTR-10 (Final Return) is due within 3 months of the date of cancellation or the cancellation order, whichever is later; the outer limit to furnish any GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B is 3 years from its due date · GSTR-2B and the Invoice Management System communicate ITC [Sec. 38] · Ledgers: ONE Electronic Liability Register (PMT-01) and TWO ledgers — Electronic Cash Ledger (PMT-05, funded by deposit) and Electronic Credit Ledger (PMT-02, credited ONLY through self-assessed ITC in a filed return, never by direct entry); Rule 86B restricts use of the credit ledger · Interest [Sec. 50] — up to 18%, and, except in proceedings u/s 73 or 74A, charged only on the portion of tax paid by debiting the Electronic Cash Ledger (the NET tax liability), never on the ITC-covered portion; interest on ITC wrongly availed AND utilised runs up to 24%.

Module 6: Customs Act & Rules (10%)

TopicThe Ladder
6.1 BasicsEntry 83 of List I empowers the Union to levy duties on imports and exports; the Customs Act, 1962 is effective from 1-2-1963 and Sec. 12 is its charging section; rates come from the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 — First Schedule for import duty, Second Schedule for export duty. Duty is on the GOODS, not on the person · Territorial waters = 12 nautical miles from the baseline, and "India" includes them; Indian Customs Waters u/s 2(28), the EEZ and the Continental Shelf all run to 200 nautical miles; 1 nautical mile = 1.1515 miles = 1.852 km · Taxable event: import commences on crossing territorial waters and completes when the goods mix with the mass of goods in India — for home consumption, when the goods reach the customs barriers and the bill of entry for home consumption is filed; for warehoused goods, on clearance for home consumption. Export is complete only when the goods cross the territorial waters — goods sinking within them are not exported · Sec. 13 pilferage after unloading and before the clearance order, not re-stored → NO duty; duty revives if the goods are re-stored, and Sec. 13 never applies once goods are warehoused · Sec. 23(1) total loss or destruction before clearance → REMISSION, the burden lying on the importer, and it DOES cover warehoused goods; where Sec. 13 applies, Sec. 23(1) does not · Sec. 22 abatement: Duty on damaged goods = (Value of the damaged goods ÷ Value before damage) × Duty before damage, the damaged value fixed by the proper officer OR by public auction/tender at the owner's option · Sec. 23(2) relinquishment of title must be UNCONDITIONAL, made before the order for clearance for home consumption or deposit in a warehouse, and is barred where an offence appears to have been committed · Sec. 19 — a set of articles liable at different ad valorem rates is chargeable wholly at the HIGHEST of those rates; accessories, spare parts and repair implements take the main article's rate · Sec. 20 — goods exported for repairs and re-imported are taxed only on the fair cost of repairs + insurance and freight both ways, provided ownership has not changed · Sec. 25 — duty is not collected where the amount leviable does not exceed ₹100; an exemption is valid up to the 31st March falling immediately after 2 years from its grant or variation · The First Schedule has 21 Sections and 98 Chapters on the WCO's HSN, used by more than 137 countries: 4 digits = heading, 6 digits = sub-heading, 8 digits = Tariff Item.
6.2 Types of dutiesSocial Welfare Surcharge = 10% of total customs duties (3% for gold and silver, including platinum-plated, unwrought, semi-manufactured or powder form), on imports ONLY — never on export. Six items are excluded from its base: Safeguard Duty, Countervailing duty on a subsidized article, Anti-dumping duty, IGST, GST Compensation Cess and AIDC — so in practice SWS is 10% of the Basic Customs Duty · IGST on imports is levied by Sec. 3(7) and GST Compensation Cess by Sec. 3(9) of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975; both use the SAME base — the Sec. 14 value plus BCD plus any sum chargeable like a duty of customs — and both exclude the IGST and the cess from that base. ITC of both is available under GST law · Safeguard measures [Sec. 8B] answer INCREASED QUANTITIES causing serious injury: provisional measures for a maximum of 200 days; the duty lapses after 4 years, extendable to 10 years; not imposed where a developing country's share is 3% or less, or all such countries together 9% or less, of total imports of that article · Countervailing duty [Sec. 9] answers a SUBSIDY and cannot exceed the amount of the subsidy · Anti-dumping duty [Sec. 9A] answers DUMPING and cannot exceed the Margin of Dumping = Normal Value − Export Price · Both run 5 years, extendable by another 5, with a further year while a review initiated before expiry is pending, and both may be levied retrospectively but not beyond 90 days from the notification; Sec. 9B bars both duties on the same situation of dumping or export subsidization.
6.3 ValuationSec. 14(1) transaction value requires five conditions: the price actually paid or payable · sold for export to or from India · delivery at the time and place of importation or exportation · buyer and seller not related · price the sole consideration. Sec. 14(2) tariff values fixed by CBIC (crude palm oil, crude palmolein, crude soyabean oil, brass scrap, poppy seeds) override it where fixed · Import hierarchy: Rule 3 (transaction) → Rule 4 (identical goods) → Rule 5 (similar goods) → Rule 7 (deductive) → Rule 8 (computed) → Rule 9 (residual). Only Rules 7 and 8 may be swapped, at the importer's request. Where more than one transaction value of identical or similar goods exists, take the LOWEST. Rule 12 is a REJECTION mechanism, not a valuation method — after rejection proceed sequentially through Rules 4 to 9 · Related persons include anyone owning, controlling or holding 5% or more of the voting rights of both, officers or directors of one another's businesses, legally recognized partners, employer and employee, one controlling the other, both controlled by a third, together controlling a third, and members of the same family — a related-party price is still accepted where the relationship did not influence it · Rule 10 ADDS: commission and brokerage other than BUYING commission, containers, packing, the buyer's free-issue materials, tools, dies and moulds, foreign engineering and design work, royalties and licence fees payable as a condition of sale, resale proceeds accruing to the seller, ship demurrage on chartered vessels and lighterage/barge charges. NOT added: buying commission, durable and returnable packing, Indian design and development work, Indian duties and taxes, port-to-factory transport and insurance, erection charges in India, unloading and landing charges at the place of importation, and port demurrage for delay in clearing · Freight: actual; if unascertained 20% of FOB; by AIR always capped at 20% of FOB even where the actual is known. Insurance: actual; if unascertained 1.125% of FOB. Backing out of a CIF figure: transport = CIF × 20/120, insurance = CIF × 1.125/101.125 · Rule 7 deductive value takes the unit price in the greatest aggregate quantity sold to UNRELATED persons — group the sales by PRICE, total the units at each price, ignore sales made more than 90 days after importation — then remember the residue is Assessable Value PLUS duty, so gross down by (100% + duty rate) · Sec. 15: the rate of duty and tariff valuation follow the bill-of-entry date, a bill of entry presented BEFORE entry inwards or arrival being deemed presented on that later date — but the exchange rate is always the CBIC rate in force on the ACTUAL date of presentation (selling rate for imports, buying rate for exports); RBI and inter-bank rates are distractors. Sec. 16: for exports the relevant date is the date of the order permitting clearance and loading u/s 51. Neither section applies to baggage or goods imported by post · Export valuation runs a shorter ladder — Rule 3 (transaction value, accepted even between related parties where the relationship did not influence the price) → Rule 4 (goods of like kind and quality) → Rule 5 (computed value) → Rule 6 (residual, where local market price may not be the ONLY basis); the Export Goods Valuation Rules, 2007 came into force on 10th October 2007, FOB is generally the price, and no Social Welfare Surcharge is levied on export.
6.4 The Master Computation Ladder — Assessable Value and the Duty Stack
Stage / RungBase it is computed on
Stage 1 — FOB (or CIF less air freight less insurance, where CIF is what you are given)as given
Add Rule 10 items not already inside → FOB value as per Customs—
Add freight (actual; if unascertained 20% of FOB; by AIR capped at 20% of FOB)FOB
Add lighterage / barge charges and ship demurrage on chartered vessels—
Add insurance (actual; if unascertained 1.125% of FOB), converted at the CBIC rate on the actual date of presentation of the bill of entryFOB
[A] CIF = ASSESSABLE VALUE—
[B] Basic Customs Duty = BCD rate × AA
[C] Social Welfare Surcharge = 10% of B (3% for gold/silver)B — never A
[D] Value for computing IGST = A + B + C (plus anti-dumping/safeguard duty and AIDC where levied)A + B + C
[E] IGST = IGST rate × DD
[F] GST Compensation Cess = cess rate × D — a PARALLEL branch from D, never stacked on top of ED
TOTAL DUTY AND TAX PAYABLE = B + C + E + F — the assessable value and the sub-total are working figures only—
Shortcut the source itself uses: BCD 12% plus SWS at 10% of BCD = an effective 13.20% of assessable valueA
The Master Trap List — The 88 Distractors This Paper Is Built From
